title: An Optimal Power-Flow Grouping Topology for Single-Isolation-Stage Multi-Output Solid-State Transformers
author: Yi Hao, Krzysztof Puczko, Levy Ferreira Costa, Liangcai Shu, Dongsheng Yang
summary: This arXiv paper proposes an interleaved submodule grouping topology for single-isolation-stage multi-output solid-state transformers, aimed at EV fast-charging and data center multi-output dc supply. The authors report reduced balancing power, lower dc-link voltage difference, and about 5.6% higher measured efficiency on a six-submodule prototype, with stable post-fault operation demonstrated.

key_insights.text: Interleaving submodules assigned to different output ports localizes power redistribution and reduces the power processed by balancing circuits compared with sequential grouping.
A six-submodule prototype showed a 63% reduction in maximum submodule dc-link voltage difference and a 14.5% reduction in peak balancing current under highly unbalanced loading.
Eliminating the separate high-power dc/dc interface stage targets lower losses for multi-output power conversion in data centers and EV charging.

title: Real-Time Nonlinear Mixed-Integer Model Predictive Control With Horizon-Tail Relaxations
author: Armin Nurkanović
summary: The paper proposes a decomposition-based model predictive control method for nonlinear systems with discrete decisions that splits mixed-integer computations before and after state measurement to cut feedback delay. It relaxes integer controls over the horizon tail and derives error bounds. In a data center cooling example, it reports a 94% reduction in mean feedback computation time versus a state-of-the-art MINLP method, with under 1% closed-loop cost difference.

key_insights.text: Solves a continuous relaxation at a predicted state before measurement arrives, then solves a mixed-integer QP once the measured state is available.
Fixes or relaxes integer controls over the prediction horizon tail while keeping an integer-feasible first control input, with derived error bounds.
In a data center cooling example, mean feedback computation time drops 94% with a closed-loop cost difference under 1%.

title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
author: Wei Wang, Himanshu Sharma, Thiagarajan Ramachandran
summary: This arXiv paper proposes an optimization framework to size a battery energy storage system that helps large data centers meet grid interconnection requirements for demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through. The model co-optimizes BESS power and energy capacity across demand response, fluctuation mitigation, and reactive voltage support, and a case study uses a real data center load profile.

key_insights.text: The framework co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across demand response, load-fluctuation mitigation, and voltage support at the point of common coupling.
Minute-level scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints and uses a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to add flexibility.
Grid requirements on flexibility, ramping, and ride-through can delay data center interconnection, and the paper aims to give guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

title: Grid-Oriented Probabilistic Load Forecasting for AI Data Centers
author: Qingyi Yao, Ding Lin, Tianqiao Zhao, Meng Yue, Jianhui Wang
summary: This arXiv paper presents an open, grid-oriented benchmark for probabilistic load forecasting of AI data centers, using measured GPU power from a 448-GPU cluster. It evaluates forecasts across probabilistic prediction, online calibration, temporal scenario generation, and reserve sizing.

key_insights.text: A quantile LightGBM forecast reached only 63.4% coverage for a nominal 90% interval after a change in cluster utilization, while online regime-conditioned calibration raised coverage to 87.3%.
Independent sampling produced unrealistic ramp distributions and excessive reserve procurement even with well-calibrated marginal forecasts.

Reconstructing temporal dependence from historical forecast errors lowered realized reserve cost by 7.4-10.6% across three forecasting tasks, suggesting marginal forecast quality alone is insufficient for operational decisions.

In the IEEE 14-bus study, the controller reduces the mean data center disconnection rate by 44.8% and grid-demand loss by 27.4% versus the best baseline.

key_insights.text: Ride-through-aware voltage control assesses voltage deviations against facility-specific voltage-duration ride-through margins under limited reactive-power support.
Incorporating data center ride-through requirements into reactive-power allocation improves data center retention and reduces grid-demand loss during faults.
In the IEEE 14-bus study, the proposed controller cuts mean data center disconnection rate by 44.8% and grid-demand loss by 27.4% versus the best-performing baseline.

The new approach supports data-dependent control flow, TMA, async operations, acquire-release synchronization, proxy fences, and megakernels, which the earlier work did not.

Commitments from OpenAI and Anthropic are cited as close to 40% of the cloud backlog.
Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion and shares fell 12.6% after its Q3 earnings call.
The cash-flow projection is built from company filings and management comments with two growth assumptions by the author, presented as rounded high-level estimates.

Power constraints are slowing delivery of new data center capacity.

title: Rondo: Controlling Reordering in High-Throughput Packet Spraying
author: Xizhi Zhang, Zhongjie Chen, Yang Zhang, Fengyuan Ren
summary: This arXiv paper presents Rondo, a packet-level multipath transport for datacenter networks that controls packet reordering under packet spraying. It combines a multipath controller using ACK-based per-path capacity estimation with a packet scheduler that compensates for persistent path-delay differences. The authors report testbed and simulation results including up to 97.5% lower maximum out-of-order degree and up to 8.51x higher goodput with constrained receiver buffers.

key_insights.text: Packet reordering under packet spraying stems from transient inter-path queueing differences caused by control dynamics and persistent path-delay differences from path heterogeneity.
Rondo pairs a multipath controller using ACK-based per-path capacity estimation and probing with a packet scheduler that adjusts transmission order to compensate for persistent delay differences.
Reported results show up to 97.5% reduction in maximum out-of-order degree and up to 8.51x higher goodput with constrained receiver buffers.

title: Nvidia orders data centre clients to reduce China exposure
author: JumpCrisscross
summary: According to an FT headline, Nvidia has instructed its data centre clients to reduce their exposure to China. The item contains no further details beyond the headline.

key_insights.text: Nvidia is directing data centre customers to reduce China exposure, per the headline.

title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks
author: Manav Mishra, Krishna M. Sivalingam
summary: An arXiv paper presents Halley, a predictive control plane for optical networks in AI data centers, aimed at handling correlated failures of lasers, switches, and microrings. The authors report simulated goodput gains and reduced data center capacity needs under the proposed approach.

key_insights.text: Correlated failures of lasers sharing an enclosure, cooling, and power can cap pool availability at a fixed spare ratio regardless of pool size.
Halley uses four components (LightReserve, FoldFit, ThermaLead, TriageGuard) with predictive control that defers to the deployed policy when uncertain.
Simulated effective goodput rises from 65.2% to 76.5% and per-megawatt training throughput is reported as up to 1.03 to 1.17 times baseline.

title: 1.26M Data Center Satellites? Orbit Says No
author: donohoe
summary: A blog post argues that orbital space is already crowded, with roughly 16,000 to 17,000 working satellites and 35,000 to 47,000 tracked objects. It states that five companies have proposed adding 1.26 million orbital data center satellites, none yet approved, and that the decisions are before the FCC.

key_insights.text: Five companies have proposed adding 1.26 million data center satellites, none of which are approved yet, and they asked to skip usual deployment deadlines.
The post says space cooling, radiation-hardened chips, and lack of in-orbit repair create physical challenges for orbital data centers.
Astronomers cited in the post put the limit on faint satellites at about 100,000, which the proposals exceed.

author: Sri Muppidi and Kalley Huang
summary: The New York Times reports on Anthropic's pursuit of AI computing power through a series of deals with tech giants, former crypto miners and other providers. The item is a headline and short excerpt, so the specific terms of the deals are not visible.

title: Grid-Mode-Aware AI Data Center Power Smoothing via Bayesian-Optimized Hybrid Energy Storage System
author: Sina Mohammadi, Quang Manh Hoang, Marcus Chen I Wada, Van-Hai Bui, Wencong Su
summary: An arXiv paper proposes a real-time control framework for a hybrid battery and supercapacitor energy storage system to smooth volatile AI data center power demand. Bayesian optimization is used offline to tune control parameters, and simulations report reduced 75-160 MW demand swings within a 10 MW band.

key_insights.text: A hybrid energy storage system combining a BESS and a supercapacitor uses frequency-decoupling and active modal damping to mitigate oscillatory AI data center load.
Offline Bayesian Optimization tunes real-time control parameters, avoiding the computational burden of online receding-horizon optimization.
Simulations report that the approach keeps AI data center demand fluctuations largely within a 10 MW target band to support grid stability.

title: Liquid Cooling Retrofits: Hard, but Sometimes Worth It
author: Christopher Tozzi
summary: The item discusses retrofitting existing data centers with liquid cooling. It says such retrofits can increase density and efficiency but involve cost, downtime, and infrastructure constraints, so they suit only certain cases.

key_insights.text: Liquid cooling retrofits carry cost and downtime trade-offs and make sense only in select cases.
Retrofitting liquid cooling can raise rack density and efficiency but is limited by existing infrastructure.

title: Ohio's Data-Center Revolt Is Upending the Midterms
author: geox
summary: Residents of Grove City, Ohio, are opposing a proposed 310-acre data center campus by Texas-based Headwaters Site Development over water, noise, energy cost, and secrecy concerns. The city passed a yearlong moratorium and voters will consider a referendum requiring voter approval for large developments, and the opposition is spreading across Ohio ahead of the midterms.

key_insights.text: Community opposition to data centers is becoming a political issue in Ohio, with Republicans and Democrats both affected ahead of the midterm elections.
Residents cite water usage, noise, energy costs and electrical infrastructure such as the substation and power lines as concerns for the proposed campus.
Grove City council passed a yearlong moratorium on data center construction, and a November ballot proposal would require voter approval for large developments.

title: Google's Minnesota data center approved after it drops $80M tax break ask
author: entryleveljobsc
summary: Google's proposed Minnesota data center has been approved after council votes were delayed twice amid local opposition. According to the headline, Google scaled down the 200-acre project and dropped its $80 million tax break request.

key_insights.text: Google withdrew its $80 million tax break request as part of a scaled-down project that won approval.
Local resident opposition delayed the council vote twice before the project moved forward.

title: Dynamic Modeling of Transmission Networks, Grid-Following Inverters, and UPS-Based AI Data Centers
author: Muhammad Hamza Ali, Amritanshu Pandey
summary: The paper presents dynamic models of a transmission network with synchronous generators and grid-following inverters, along with average models of AI data centers. Each data center includes an IT load driven by a measured GPU power trace, an induction-motor cooling load, and a double-conversion UPS with battery and converters. The authors describe smooth surrogates for non-smooth operations and how each model is initialized at its power-flow operating point.

key_insights.text: AI data centers are modeled with an IT load driven by a measured GPU power trace, an induction-motor cooling load, and a constant-impedance load.
A double-conversion UPS serving the IT load is modeled with rectifier, grid-forming output inverter, battery, and bidirectional DC-DC converter.
Non-smooth operations are replaced with smooth surrogates so the discretized model stays continuously differentiable for the nonlinear solver.

author: roschdal
summary: A headline reports that a Google data center construction project recorded 143 regulatory violations. The linked article, from Aftenposten, is not available here, so details are unconfirmed.

title: Optimizing 124B MoE inference on a single Nvidia DGX Spark
author: trcytony
summary: NVIDIA's developer blog describes three techniques for speeding up inference of the Ling-3.0-flash mixture-of-experts model on a single DGX Spark: Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels, online FP8 quantization of the LM head, and multi-token prediction speculative decoding with NEXTN. The post reports that decoding was memory-bound and notes an integration issue that can make the combined configuration slower than baseline.

key_insights.text: Profiling showed batch-size-1 decoding on DGX Spark was memory-bound, with reading model weights driving execution time.
Online FP8 quantization of the LM head halves the weight-read volume for that layer, which is a high-value target under a bandwidth bottleneck.
Humming compiles kernels at runtime via NVRTC for specific shapes, so individual kernels build in seconds versus tens of minutes for the FlashInfer CUTLASS path.
The post frames single-workstation inference optimization as a way to generate tokens faster on constrained hardware.

title: Flare, Nvidia's DGX Spark Inference Engine
author: jacquesm

Site rankings are based on internal rate of return, linking location choice to investment returns.

title: A History of Nvidia Stream Multiprocessor (2020)
author: andsoitis
summary: A technical walkthrough of the evolution of Nvidia's stream multiprocessor (SM) architecture, from the 2006 unified Tesla G80 through Fermi, Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal and Turing. The author describes how the unified design replaced fixed-function vertex, fragment and geometry stages and explains SIMT warp execution, SFU units, register file and float64 limitations.

key_insights.text: The unified Tesla architecture replaced separate vertex, fragment and geometry stages with Stream Multiprocessors that run any kernel type, letting load balance shift automatically with the pipeline's needs.
Warps of 32 threads execute in SIMT fashion, and performance depends on hiding memory latency with schedulable warps and avoiding control-flow divergence.
The G80 had no hardware float64 support, so double-precision work was done in software with a large speed penalty.

title: A Compute Center Anyone Can Join: A Peer-to-Peer System for AI Inference
author: Yimo Lin, Zhen Zhang
summary: This arXiv paper proposes the Open Inference Market, a peer-to-peer system where individuals and small institutions contribute GPU capacity for AI inference. It uses earnings held as collateral during a challenge window to deter cheating, and presents a simplified model of audit requirements and deterrence.

key_insights.text: The number of audits needed for deterrence is stated to be a constant per worker per day, independent of throughput, so the audited share falls as the network grows busier.
Whether the mechanism works depends on the ratio of the audit judge's false-flag rate to its detection rate.
Idle GPUs owned by individuals and small institutions could be monetized for AI inference through an economic mechanism instead of a central operator.

title: Hermantown approves controversial Google Data Center during late night meeting

Google made concessions before the vote, including dropping a request for up to $80 million in property tax breaks and reducing the project from four buildings to three.

key_insights.text: Google dropped a request for up to $80 million in property tax breaks and the project is now estimated to provide about $3 million annually in property tax revenue to Hermantown.
The approvals include a $210 million decommissioning agreement intended to protect the city if the project is scrapped or abandoned.
The project was reduced from four buildings to three, with building height capped at 33 feet, and Google agreed to monitor private wells near the site.
Local opposition led to meeting cancellations, restricted attendance of 85 people, and closure of an overflow room, with opponents criticizing the process.

title: Clockwork: Scheduling Compound AI Systems in Space Data Centers
author: Milos Gravara, Andrija Stanisic, Stefan Nastic
summary: The paper presents Clockwork, a framework for scheduling Compound AI workflows on LEO-based space data centers under end-to-end latency SLOs. It has two components, Castor for selecting active orbital planes and component placements per constellation snapshot, and Pollux for building a low-cost schedule across predicted orbital evolution. The authors report serving 81% of instances at a 300 ms SLO and a 56% mean reduction in scheduling cost versus heuristic baselines.

key_insights.text: Provisioning for space data centers must be planned over time because orbital motion changes which satellites can serve an area of interest, and placement changes or plane activations carry costs.
Castor jointly selects active orbital planes and component placements for each constellation snapshot, while Pollux links candidate states across predicted orbital evolution.
On the experimental two-shell constellation, Pollux reduces mean total scheduling cost by 56% on average and up to 63% compared to heuristic baselines.

The claim is presented as evidence that domestic Chinese chipmakers are closing the technology gap with Nvidia.

Nvidia provided $3.1 billion to Nscale through unsecured convertible loan notes received September 15, per the S-1.

title: Winners and Losers If the Data Center Buildout Is Delayed
author: akyuu
summary: Apollo's Daily Spark piece analyzes who would win and lose if the data center buildout is delayed, given compute demand exceeding supply. It argues owners of operating capacity, powered land, long-lead equipment makers and power producers would benefit, while hyperscaler earnings growth, developers, and AI-linked equities would be hurt.

key_insights.text: Operating data centers and holders of powered land with grid access benefit from scarcity, since new competitors cannot arrive quickly.
A delay pushes developer cash flows out while interest and carrying costs continue, with leveraged or pre-lease-dependent developers facing refinancing stress.
Lead times for transformers can reach up to 26 months, giving long-lead equipment makers pricing power.
The investment distinction is delay versus cancellation: a delay pushes cash flows out, while scarcity could unwind if supply catches up or demand softens.

title: Ordered Chaos: Towards Adaptive Multipath Load Balancing with Precise Fast Loss Detection
author: Tommaso Bonato, Ahmad Ghalayini, Nadeen Gebara, Benoit Pit-Claudel, Jiayong Li, Mikhail Khalilov, Luca Piccolboni, Waleed Reda, Pei-Huan Tsai, Tao Ji et al.
summary: This arXiv paper proposes Ordered Chaos, an end-host multipath load balancing design for best-effort datacenter fabrics that splits flows into ordered, dynamically routed subflows. It adds Precise Fast Loss Detection, which uses probes to distinguish reordering from congestion, corruption, tail, and retransmission losses within one RTT. The authors report simulation, AI/HPC workload, and DPU prototype results, including up to 3x better tail flow completion time and up to 35% faster collective and training communication.

key_insights.text: Packet spraying balances load well but removes the ordering signals needed for fast, precise loss detection, while ECMP keeps loss semantics but uses path diversity coarsely.
Reactive Subflow Spraying divides each flow into ordered, dynamically routed subflows, and Precise Fast Loss Detection uses probes to classify loss causes within one RTT.
Reported results include up to 3x improvement in tail flow completion time and up to 35% acceleration of collective and training communication for AI and HPC workloads.

title: Electrocutions, Intimidation and Wage Theft Haunt Europe's Data Center Workers
author: cdrnsf
summary: An Investigate Europe investigation, published with Tech Policy Press, reports on hazardous working conditions for workers building Europe's AI data center infrastructure. It centers on an arc flash electrocution of an electrical tester at a Google data center site in Saint-Ghislain, Belgium, after a last-minute request to run tests on live lines.

key_insights.text: Belgium's federal labor inspectorate closed its investigation into the accident without finding wrongdoing, and no fines or sanctions are known to have been issued.
The worker was asked to perform tests on electrical lines that were supposed to be de-energized, but were live, and he did not retrieve the protective suit because of time pressure.
Subcontracted labor on the Google campus, including Dornan Engineering and a recruitment agency, is part of the worker safety and accountability picture.

key_insights.text: Metro sites, not towers, are described as the clearest near-term edge AI opportunity for telecoms.

title: Multi-Timescale Deliverability of Shared Hybrid Storage for AI Data Center Campuses
author: Zihan Meng, Ruizhang Yang, Chenxi Hu, Francis Yunhe Hou
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a multi-timescale scheduling model for a shared hybrid energy storage system that mitigates power fluctuations at an AI data center campus. The model separates commanded from delivered power at the campus point of common coupling and is evaluated with the NLR GenAI Power Profiles Dataset, reporting reduced PCC and fast integral absolute error.

key_insights.text: A two-layer model passes five-minute scheduled power, energy state, and reserve capacity to a causal fast response model that distinguishes commanded from delivered power.
Case studies show reductions in both PCC and fast integral absolute error while retaining most of the improvement available under ideal response.
Shared storage at the campus bus constrains the system to a single point of common coupling injection, relevant to how AI campuses manage grid-facing power variability.

title: Market Efficiency and Capacity Investment under Flexible Price-Making Loads: A Computational Study
author: Aron Brenner, Deepjyoti Deka, Saurabh Amin
summary: An arXiv study models a large flexible load such as a data center as a price-making consumer leading the system operator in a Stackelberg game. It compares the consumer's temporal and spatial load shifting with a cost-minimizing planner's over a simulated RTS-GMLC year. The authors report strategic shifting captures 75% (temporal) and 93% (spatial) of planner savings, and relate flexibility to thermal capacity, transmission, and renewables.

key_insights.text: Strategic temporal and spatial shifting capture 75% and 93% of the planner's savings, with the remainder mostly forgone by withholding flexibility to protect favorable prices.
Scarce capacity and abundant renewables raise the share captured by temporal shifting, while scarce transmission lowers the share captured by spatial shifting.
Temporal and spatial flexibility act as substitutes for thermal and transmission capacity, respectively, and complement renewables.

title: Advanced Matrix Multiplication Optimization on Nvidia GPUs
author: skidrow
summary: A write-up describes an open-source CUDA implementation of single-precision matrix multiplication (SGEMM) for NVIDIA GPUs, tuned on an RTX 3090. It covers optimizations such as inlined PTX, asynchronous memory copies, double-buffering, and shared memory bank-conflict avoidance, and compares performance against cuBLAS and other implementations.

key_insights.text: The kernel uses inlined PTX, asynchronous memory copies, double-buffering, and avoidance of shared memory bank conflicts.
Performance is benchmarked against cuBLAS and Simon Boehm's tinyBLAS with locked and unlocked GPU clocks, and the implementation was tuned on an RTX 3090.
The project is aimed mainly at CUDA learners rather than at outperforming cuBLAS on all GPUs and matrix sizes.

The authors report that moratoriums are the most common instrument (1,010 counted, averaging 10 months) and that policy shifted from tax incentives toward bans and restrictions starting around October 2025.

Since around October 2025, most policies have shifted from tax incentives to bans and restrictions, which the authors link to higher energy prices and worsening public sentiment toward AI.
Where construction is allowed, protections are most often placed on electricity and less often on water.

key_insights.text: The tool calculates coolant temperature rise, pressure drop and pump operating point for liquid cold plates.
It produces a 2D temperature map for thermal analysis.

title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets
author: Bole Ma, Ayesha Afzal, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Koestler, Gerhard Wellein
summary: An arXiv paper measures the energy cost of speculative decoding for LLM serving on H100 and H200 GPUs under SGLang with CUDA graphs, across batch sizes up to 64 and five corpora. It finds that energy savings depend on draft acceptance rate, shrink as batch size grows, and can become a loss at large batches with block drafters.

key_insights.text: On dense models, verification rather than drafting dominates the energy cost of speculative decoding.
At large batch sizes, block drafters push verification into the compute-bound regime, where speculation's energy saving becomes a loss.
Meeting a tighter latency target with speculation can cost additional energy, which affects tokens served per unit of facility power.
Larger batches lower energy per token without speculation, and speculation adds to that saving only when acceptance is high.

title: Texas Data Center Boom Collides with Backlash Ahead of Midterms

summary: A Bloomberg headline reports that the Texas data center boom is colliding with local backlash ahead of the midterm elections. No article text is available, so details beyond the headline are not known.

summary: The NAACP presents a public education dashboard that lets users enter an address to see candidates on their ballot, their stances on climate issues, and nearby upcoming projects, policies, and data center locations. title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute
author: Jiansheng Wang, Jaskeerat Singh, Haochen Xu, Xinyi Li, Mingyuan Yan, Shaohui Liu, Yuzhuo Li, Yize Chen, Wenqi Cui
summary: The arXiv paper introduces LLM-PowerTrace, an open dataset of time-resolved, per-GPU power traces sampled every 100 ms across NVIDIA platforms for LLM fine-tuning and inference, with workload and system metadata. It also defines power-grid-facing metrics and an AI-compute power and energy scaling law for extrapolation beyond measured settings.

key_insights.text: Existing LLM energy benchmarks report aggregate quantities such as joules per token and rarely release underlying time-series measurements.
The dataset profiles per-GPU power traces every 100 ms across fine-tuning and inference sweeps including batch size, precision, concurrency, GPU frequency, and quantization.

title: Data Center Load Reductions: Attribution, Measurement Limits, and Estimation
author: Abdallah Alalem Albustami, Ahmad F. Taha, Mohammad Alwahdanee, Zuhaib Shakeel Muhammad
summary: This arXiv paper examines how to tell whether a sudden data center load reduction was caused by a workload change or a switch to backup supply, using point-of-interconnection measurements. It finds the two mechanisms can look identical in quasi-static models, and proposes a workload-data-based estimator when POI data are insufficient.

key_insights.text: Workload reduction and switching to backup supply can produce identical POI voltage and current in a quasi-static constant power model.
During transients, separation of the two mechanisms depends on reduction size relative to measurement noise, clearing time, workload dynamics, and recorder bandwidth.
NERC calls on transmission owners to install disturbance recorders at data center facilities to support root cause analysis of load reductions.

title: Machine learning-guided real-time AC optimal transmission switching
author: Weimin Huang, Weiwei Yang, Bistra Dilkina, Konstantina Mellou, Ishai Menache, Marco Molinaro, Chris White, Baosen Zhang
summary: The paper presents a machine learning-guided method for real-time AC optimal transmission switching, using a fine-tuned surrogate model to guide search over transmission line topologies. Candidate switching decisions are verified with exact AC-OPF solvers within a 50-second budget. On a 2,000-bus synthetic Texas grid under a data center buildout scenario, the authors report a 31.97% generation cost reduction and a 94.34% reduction in gross nodal load payments.

key_insights.text: A fine-tuned pretrained AC-OPF model estimates generation-cost reduction from opening transmission lines to guide combinatorial topology search.
Candidate topologies are verified with exact AC-OPF solvers, so the surrogate does not need to guarantee feasibility.
Under a realistic data center buildout scenario on a 2,000-bus synthetic Texas grid, the approach reports a 31.97% generation cost reduction and a 94.34% reduction in gross nodal load payments.

title: Opportunistic Optical Link Scheduling in the Scalable Matching Model

It evaluates OOLS within the Scalable Matching Model using simulations with synthetic and real-world datacenter workloads. The authors report substantial gains in communication cost and throughput.

key_insights.text: Bounded-degree reconfigurable networks use only a small portion of OCS infrastructure at a given time when port count is much smaller than the number of switches, especially under skewed and bursty traffic.
OOLS leverages idle OCS resources to augment bounded-degree reconfigurable topologies.
Simulation results indicate lower communication costs and higher throughput for datacenter workloads.

title: Context Is Not Free: Carbon-Aware LLM Routing for Multi-Turn LLM Web Services across Geo-Distributed Data Centers
author: Xiaoyang Zhang, Yuejun Yan, Qingang Zhang, Yonggang Wen

It adds a cache-aware carbon cost model that accounts for recomputing KV-cache history when a session moves, and reports a 16.1% average CO2 reduction relative to FairCarbon in trace-driven experiments.

key_insights.text: Moving a multi-turn conversation to another deployment requires recomputing its KV-cache history, whose carbon cost grows with conversation length and can outweigh routing savings.
A lightweight gate keeps a session on its cached deployment when it would likely move back and rebuild history at the next turn.
Reported carbon reduction is 16.1% on average versus FairCarbon, rising to 23.1% for sessions longer than 30 turns, with predicted answer quality and estimated latency also improved.

title: LLMs in Cloud: A Discussion on Architecture, Orchestration, and Inference
author: Jannatun Noor, Athar Noor Mohammad Rafee, Md. Sadman Haque, Sreezon Das Gupta, Atiar Osman, Md. Abu Obaida Zishan
summary: This arXiv paper presents a cross-layer systematic review (PRISMA 2020 framework) of LLM serving in cloud datacenters, covering hardware virtualization, cluster scheduling, and runtime inference optimizations. It also evaluates serverless, checkpointing, and trusted execution environment architectures and outlines Pareto trade-offs among throughput, latency, cost, and confidentiality, along with a research roadmap.

key_insights.text: Serving large models faces bottlenecks including the HBM wall, the asymmetry between compute-bound prefilling and memory-bandwidth-bound decoding, and KV cache expansion.
The review covers continuous batching, prefill-decoding disaggregation, and hierarchical KV cache offloading as runtime optimizations.

title: How AI Load Swings Reduce Datacenter Power Conversion Efficiency
author: Heetarth Joshi, Ali Alenezi, Fang Chen Lin, Prasad Enjeti, Xiaoyang Wang, Xin Chen
summary: An arXiv paper quantifies how repeated GPU power swings between compute and communication phases reduce efficiency in cascaded rack power conversion. Using an energy-based, cycle-averaged method and measured GaN PFC and LLC converter curves on a 240 V AC to 400 V DC to 51 V DC path, it reports a 0.88% loss for a 1 Hz swinging load and 1.66% when point-of-load conversion to the chip rail is included. The authors conclude that efficiency rated at average load overstates real-world performance.

key_insights.text: For a 1 Hz, 50% duty-cycle load swinging between 5 kW and 510 W, conversion efficiency falls to 95.97% versus 96.82% at the equivalent constant average load, a 0.88% loss.
Including 51/48V to 1V point-of-load conversion to the chip rail raises the loss to 1.66% (89.45% vs. 90.96%).
Efficiency rated at average load overstates real-world performance, and the penalty grows with each load-dependent conversion stage between the grid and the GPU.

title: Modeling Liquid-Cooled Data Centers in EnergyPlus

summary: An arXiv paper presents a native EnergyPlus object that models direct-to-chip liquid cooling for chilled-water and warm-water architectures within whole-building simulations. The authors validate it against a Modelica implementation across 21 operating conditions and report a case study where warm-water liquid cooling lowers annual PUE from 1.43 to 1.25 compared with an air-cooled baseline.

key_insights.text: The EnergyPlus object couples facility-water loops, rack-side secondary loops, coolant distribution units, and chip-junction temperatures in a single solver.
Validation reports loop-temperature RMSE at or below 0.021 K against a 0.1 K acceptance threshold, including two full-year runs at one-minute resolution.
The case study reports warm-water liquid cooling reduces annual PUE from 1.43 to 1.25 and cuts total facility energy by 37.9% versus air cooling.

title: Embodied Emissions of 2.5D and 3D Scaling in Chipletized GPUs for Low-Carbon AI
author: Hannah Watson, Arjun Singh, Jennifer Stephenson, Job Soethoudt, Jonas Svedas, Debjyoti Bhattacharjee, James Myers
summary: An arXiv paper estimates the embodied emissions of a chiplet-based GPU scaled with 2.5D and 3D packaging using the imec.netzero modelling platform. Doubling compute units and HBM capacity, the authors report an 89% EE increase for 3D scaling versus 141% for 2.5D scaling.

key_insights.text: 3D scaling of a chiplet-based GPU produced an 89% increase in embodied emissions when compute units and HBM capacity were doubled, compared with 141% for 2.5D scaling.
The authors position 3D scaling as a way to limit embodied emissions from GPU scaling in hyperscale data centers.

title: Nvidia Sentry: Secure AI Agents at Runtime
author: hasheddan
summary: NVIDIA describes Sentry, a security framework that monitors AI agents and enforces policies on their access to models, tools, and data from outside the host. It runs on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs as part of the OpenShell reference architecture and uses DOCA Flow and DOCA Tower to firewall and inspect agent traffic at layers 4 and 7.

key_insights.text: NVIDIA Sentry runs on BlueField-4 DPUs in a separate hardware trust domain, so agents and host software cannot alter or disable its monitoring and enforcement.
DOCA Flow implements a per-agent layer-4 firewall in silicon, and forwards permitted traffic to DOCA Tower, an Envoy-based transparent proxy that performs layer-7 inspection and TLS termination.
Agent network traffic reaches BlueField-4 through a direct network I/O path that bypasses host OS and hypervisor packet processing.
The framework targets enterprises deploying autonomous AI agents that need enforceable access controls on models, tools, and data.

title: Beyond Hotness: High-Resolution Memory Characterization of Cloud and LLM Workloads for Tiered Memory with ARM SPE
author: Jie Ren, Ivy Peng
summary: The paper presents a high-resolution memory characterization methodology using ARM's Statistical Profiling Extension to study tiered memory usage. It analyzes eight memory-intensive cloud and LLM workloads from CloudSuite and proposes metrics based on memory idle periods and latency profiles for data placement.

key_insights.text: The methodology is implemented with ARM's Statistical Profiling Extension (SPE) and applied to eight memory-intensive CloudSuite and LLM workloads.
New metrics based on memory idle periods and latency profiles are proposed to determine suitable data placement for tiered memory.
Memory demand from data analytics and LLM workloads is driving up memory costs in cloud and data centers, motivating multi-tier memory.

title: Nvidia caused the gaming GPU shortage by pushing AI stockpiling
author: entryleveljobsc

It cites reports from Ed Zitron, Bloomberg and Business Insider, and describes a possible channel-stuffing dynamic and future oversupply risk.

key_insights.text: Reported AWS purchases of Nvidia chips (about $5B in August with roughly $3B per month in further commitments) are said to be waiting on utility power upgrades and data center construction.
Analysts quoted in the article suggest Nvidia may be channel stuffing enterprise orders, shifting storage, power, and depreciation burdens to buyers.
The article says gaming GPUs and data center GPUs rely on the same TSMC manufacturing nodes, linking wafer allocation to the consumer shortage.

title: Can Evaporative Cooling in Data Centers Still Make Sense?
author: Andy Patrizio
summary: The article asks whether evaporative cooling still makes sense for data centers. It notes that the method is hard to defend on water-use grounds, but some operators still choose it for lower upfront cost, higher efficiency, and dry-climate performance.

key_insights.text: Some operators still choose evaporative cooling despite water-use concerns, citing lower upfront cost.
Evaporative cooling is described as offering higher efficiency and performing well in dry climates.

title: Heterogeneous Space Data Centers: A Key Paradigm for Future Non-Terrestrial and In-Orbit Services
author: Peng Hu, Mustafa Alhassan, Amjad Iqbal
summary: This arXiv paper proposes heterogeneous space-based data centers made of large and small orbital nodes that provide AI computing and communication services. It analyzes solar power availability, visibility windows, latency-aware coverage, and energy requirements for low-Earth orbit configurations.

key_insights.text: The paper analyzes solar power availability, visibility windows, and latency-aware coverage for dawn-dusk LEO configurations.
Heterogeneous space data center nodes are differentiated by computing capability, size, and power budget, with space-to-space and space-to-ground interconnection topologies.
The paper provides design guidance on trade-offs among node size, orbit selection, and service portfolio for AI infrastructure in space.

title: Democratizing LLM Training with the Edge: Challenges, Systems, and the Road Ahead
author: Ziyue Luo, Jiaxuan Cai, Cedric LeDenmat, Srijith Nair, Fatemeh Nourzad, Rohith Krishnan, Qinhang Wu, Jifan Zhang, Sungjae Lee, Zhe Li et al.
summary: This arXiv paper examines distributed LLM training across heterogeneous clients and geo-distributed sites as an alternative to centralized GPU data centers. It proposes a unified architecture with a cloud-hosted parameter server, outbound gRPC connections, and shared communication, compression, and fault-tolerance components. The authors report experiments training GPT-2 Medium and Llama3-1B across multiple university sites and outline open problems.

key_insights.text: The proposed architecture uses a cloud-hosted parameter server that coordinates heterogeneous clients over outbound gRPC connections.
One communication, compression, and fault-tolerance stack is reused for both pretraining and several fine-tuning methods.
Real geo-distributed experiments on GPT-2 Medium and Llama3-1B pretraining reportedly showed stable convergence under realistic conditions.
Centralized LLM development is described as hard to sustain, while smaller institutions holding private data lack comparable infrastructure.

title: The Shortage Won't Break Nvidia. The Labs Might

It cites recent selloffs in neoclouds and NVIDIA, widening credit signals on CoreWeave, and the high-bandwidth memory supply that still constrains accelerators.

key_insights.text: CoreWeave and Nebius fell about 30% since October 8, while NVIDIA fell about 10%, with CoreWeave's default insurance hitting a record.
The author argues the critical question is whether compute renters, including AI labs, can keep paying, not what happens to rental rates when the shortage ends.
High-bandwidth memory stacked on GPUs is still described as tight, even as commodity DRAM supply may loosen.

title: Nvidia launches Minerva to catch failing parts in giant AI data centres

The software groups related alerts into single incidents with a likely cause and includes an AI assistant that suggests fixes. IREN, Bitdeer AI, IBM, Jio, Lambda and Tesla plan to use it, and Dell, Lenovo and Supermicro will offer it; Nvidia did not disclose pricing.

key_insights.text: Minerva correlates telemetry from GPUs, network gear, storage, schedulers and workloads into one map, allowing a slow job to be traced to the causing component.
Machine learning learns normal behavior and predicts failures, and related alerts are grouped into a single incident with a likely cause.
Nvidia is extending its push beyond chips into software for operators building AI data centers, with OEM partners Dell, Lenovo and Supermicro offering it to customers.

title: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective
author: Haotian Zheng, Zhanwei Wang, Kaibin Huang
summary: An arXiv paper proposes SpaceWPT, a framework that uses inter-satellite laser wireless power transfer to redistribute solar power among satellites hosting mixture-of-experts LLM inference in space data centers. The authors derive a two-sided water-filling strategy to balance power between donor and receiver satellites under transfer losses. Simulations with Mixtral-8x7B and Phi-3.5-MoE report up to 29.25% lower inference latency than without power transfer.

key_insights.text: Skewed expert activation in MoE inference creates uneven power demand across satellites despite uniform solar supply in a dawn-dusk SSO.
A two-sided water-filling strategy decides whether each active expert donates, retains, or receives power based on water level and WPT link efficiency.
Simulations report up to 29.25% lower inference latency versus no WPT, with larger gains for more compact formations and higher transfer efficiencies.

The abstract reports preserving 95.7% of training throughput, restoring stalled inference, and achieving 4.7x MRC's simulated bandwidth.

key_insights.text: OMRC remaps collectives and circuits to handle network failures in direct-connect optical datacenters.
The abstract reports 95.7% training throughput preserved and 4.7x simulated bandwidth relative to MRC.

title: Running ClickHouse on Nvidia Vera CPU

The post describes Vera's core, cache, and memory bandwidth specs and outlines micro-benchmarks for filter, aggregation, and join operations to test how well ClickHouse scales on the platform.

key_insights.text: NVIDIA Vera is a two-socket system with 176 cores and 352 hardware threads, with up to 1.0 to 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth depending on DRAM capacity.
ClickHouse tests scalability by checking whether query speed grows linearly with core count, cache, and memory bandwidth, using an in-memory dataset to avoid disk I/O bottlenecks.
The post notes agentic AI queries are ad-hoc, bursty, and run in large parallel numbers, a workload pattern that shapes database hardware demands.

title: D-Pingmesh: Dynamic Probing and Fault Localization for Reconfigurable Datacenter Networks
author: Yunze Wei, Kaicheng Yang, Xiaohui Xie, Dunkai Mao, Peiying Tao, Yikai Zhao, Bolong Cui, Chen Sun, Bingyang Liu, Kun Tan et al.
summary: D-Pingmesh is a probing and fault-localization system for reconfigurable datacenter networks that co-designs pinglist generation with the topology and traffic engineering control plane. The paper reports fewer probing tasks than Pingmesh, faster pinglist generation than RD-Probe, and improved micro F1 in ns-3 simulation over the deTector PLL baseline, plus a testbed deployment.

key_insights.text: Control-plane-aware pinglist generation greedily admits probes with high interface coverage under the current TPE/TE snapshot.
Incremental replay-and-repair updates pinglists across reconfigurations instead of recomputing from scratch.
A Rho-EM localizer jointly infers old/new-path mixture weights and the fault set at control-plane boundaries, improving micro F1 from 0.871 to 0.953 in simulation.
At a 0.99 coverage target, the system uses 17.7x fewer tasks than Pingmesh on an 8-pod reconfigurable topology.

title: Data Center Oscillation Isolation and Grid Support: Fundamental Limits and Source-Selective Control
author: Cheng Feng
summary: The paper derives fundamental limits and designs a source-selective storage controller to isolate oscillations caused by fluctuating data center computing demand while providing prescribed grid support. The controller is designed via convex frequency-domain optimization and is tested on a single-generator interconnection and a modified nine-bus network.

key_insights.text: A coupled closed-loop model shows a direct isolation-support conflict when only grid-import-power feedback is used.
Additional electrical measurements can remove the pointwise conflict but leave a conditional cross-frequency sensitivity limit.
The local residual-feedback storage controller outperforms equal-order optimized comparators in oscillation isolation on the test networks while meeting grid response requirements.

title: PlaneZip: Lossless Bit-Plane Compression of Training Activations Offloaded over PCIe
author: Zhufan Gu, Qizhe Tang, Yuxin Wang, Xun Zhou, Hui Feng
summary: This arXiv paper presents PlaneZip, a lossless bit-plane compression scheme for GPU training activations that are swapped to host memory over PCIe. The authors report compression ratios and simulated reductions in rematerialization overhead relative to a bandwidth-aware planner and the MegTaiChi cost model.

key_insights.text: A per-128-byte-block codec selects the smallest of zero-value, delta bit-plane, bit-plane, and zero-masked bit-plane encodings to compress swapped activations.
Compressing activations on the copy path lets the planner budget link time in compressed transfer times, changing when swapping beats recomputation.
Simulated results claim a 47% and 31% cut in rematerialization overhead versus a bandwidth-aware planner without compression, with an estimated engine area of 0.036 square millimeters.

title: Degradation Aware V2G Dispatch for Co-Optimization of Parking Facility and Edge Data Center Located in the Airport Campus

V2G is reported to cut more peak demand per dollar of investment than a 5 MW/10 MWh stationary battery and needs no extra land, with payback within 10 years if bidirectional chargers cost under about $1800 more.

title: Nvidia RTX Pro 4500 Blackwell Server: L40S Throughput at 165W in a Single Slot

title: Converter-Aware Coordination of Computing Flexibility in Behind-the-Meter Data Centers
author: Ruolan Cui, Ruizhang Yang, Chenxi Hu, Franxis Yunhe Hou
summary: The paper proposes a converter-aware intraday scheduling method for behind-the-meter data centers that coordinates computing workloads with photovoltaic generation, energy storage, and grid purchases while respecting converter and network voltage limits. The authors model tasks with a mixed-integer formulation and a four-node electrical model using second-order cone relaxation. Case studies report that coordinated scheduling achieves negligible inference shortage and passes verification against the original AC model, whereas fixed training cannot support full inference service within voltage limits.

key_insights.text: Ignoring converter and network operating limits can cause converter overloads, protection trips, and interruptions to power and computing services.
Minkowski-sum aggregation and Shapley-Folkman convexification yield a linear inference-pool representation without unit-level binary variables.
Coordinating workload flexibility with on-site PV, storage, and grid purchases reduces grid dependence in behind-the-meter data centers.

title: Data Center Load Accommodation under QoS and Checkpoint-Induced Frequency Security Constraints
author: Ruolan Cui, Ziang Liu, Chenxi Hu, Francis Yunhe Hou
summary: This arXiv paper proposes an optimal data center load accommodation method that jointly considers workload quality of service, checkpoint-induced frequency security, and grid adequacy. The authors report that the method avoids a 40.3% overestimation of accommodable capacity compared with a grid-adequacy benchmark. They find QoS is the main limiting factor and that frequency-security constraints tighten as training workloads grow.

key_insights.text: Synchronized checkpointing of training workloads can cause large, rapid load reductions that threaten grid frequency stability.
Case studies show QoS is the primary limiting factor on data center load accommodation, while checkpoint-induced frequency-security constraints become more restrictive as training workloads increase.
Grid-adequacy-only assessments can overestimate accommodable data center capacity by 40.3%, so interconnection planning should also account for QoS and frequency-security risks.

key_insights.text: The AIStore ETL API deserialized user-supplied Kubernetes PodSpecs and forwarded them to the Kubernetes API without inspecting SecurityContext attributes.
Validate() checked operational constraints such as readiness probes and ports but not security settings like privileged and hostPID.

title: DC-TORQ: Fast Assessment of Data Center-Induced Generator Torsional Oscillation Risk Quantification
author: Yingyi Tang, Bin Wang, Junbo Zhao, Qiang Zhang, Pradip Vijayan, Xiaochuan Luo, Tongxin Zheng
summary: The paper proposes an analytical framework for assessing how periodic power oscillations from large data centers can excite turbine-generator shaft torsional modes. It derives closed-form transfer functions from data center power perturbations to shaft torque and uses them to set frequency-dependent limits and a screening criterion for connection buses. The method is validated on the IEEE benchmark model and applied to the IEEE 39-bus system.

key_insights.text: Data center periodic power demand can introduce forced oscillations that excite generator shaft torsional modes when frequency components are near a turbine-generator torsional mode.
Closed-form transfer functions map data center power perturbations to torque in each shaft section, avoiding repeated EMT simulations across frequencies and load locations.
The framework provides a quantitative screening criterion for choosing candidate data center connection buses.

title: Identifiability-Guided Composite Load Modeling of AI Data Centers
author: Ding Lin, Jianhui Wang, Meng Yue, Tianqiao Zhao
summary: The paper proposes an identifiability-guided calibration framework for a composite load model of AI data centers with IT, cooling, and auxiliary branches, for use in power-system transient stability studies. It evaluates the approach on 300,000 MIT Supercloud GPU power samples and 12,600 IEEE 39-bus fault scenarios, reporting higher aggregate and transient accuracy than an LSTM baseline.

key_insights.text: A workload non-equivalence result shows that voltage-only recalibration cannot reproduce workload-dependent responses of AI data center loads.
Branch-level supervision preserves relatively high aggregate accuracy but substantially degrades cooling-component recovery when removed.
Under unseen deep voltage sags, the proposed model achieves a transient R² of 0.750 versus 0.033 for the LSTM baseline.

title: BIER-DC: Stateless Multicast for In-Orbit Space Data Centers in LEO Constellations

summary: This arXiv paper evaluates how satellite cluster sizes affect visibility and gateway outage for space data centers in LEO constellations. It proposes BIER-DC, a stateless one-to-many multicast protocol that separates inter-cluster forwarding from intra-cluster delivery.

key_insights.text: BIER-DC encodes compact cluster-level forwarding information in packet headers to reduce header length and byte-hop overhead.
The protocol is compared against BIER, BIER-TE, and Yeti, with reported improvements in effective goodput and scalability.
Terrestrial cloud regions may give satellite data high delivery latency due to intermittent satellite-to-ground visibility.

title: A Critical Review of Grid Integration Challenges and Flexibility Opportunities for Large-Scale Data Centers
author: Bibek Dhakal, Manohar Chamana, Biswambhar Gayen, Jatendar Kumar, S M Shams Rahman, Aaqib Peerzada, Ki Yeob Lee, Olatunji M. Adeyanju, Bhaskar Mitra, Stephen Bayne
summary: This arXiv review examines how large-scale data centers integrate with electric grids, covering resource planning, large-load interconnection, distribution feeders, market operation, power quality and asset management. It compares load modeling approaches and assesses flexibility options such as UPS and battery control, workload flexibility, renewable co-location and clean firm supply. The central finding is that peak demand and annual energy matching alone cannot establish reliable or sustainable integration.

key_insights.text: Data centers combine high rack densities, converter-dominated interfaces, thermally coupled cooling and UPS systems, which distinguish them from conventional commercial loads.
Distribution-level issues such as harmonic resonance, ride-through and reconnection, transformer derating, cable ampacity and neutral-conductor heating receive particular attention.

Credible grid assessment must consider hourly and locational supply, network deliverability, marginal emissions, backup obligations and verified operating capability, not only requested peak demand and annual energy matching.

key_insights.text: The project validates the barometer with factor regressions, GARCH/DCC models, Diebold-Yilmaz connectedness, event-study analysis and GSADF exuberance tests in R.
The barometer tracks stock market performance across the data center value chain, framed as market intelligence.

title: Impact of Security Modeling Fidelity on Hyperscale Data Center Hosting Capacity Assessment
author: Haoxiang Wan, Linhan Fang, Jonghwan Kwon, Jesus Silva-Rodriguez, Jianyi Yang, Jaya Yellajosula, Fan Jiang, Xingpeng Li
summary: This arXiv paper defines data center hosting capacity as the maximum time-invariant active power demand at a single bus over a 24-hour peak-day horizon. It compares four grid models of increasing fidelity on a modified IEEE 24-bus system. The authors report that the N-SCUC model yields an average of 444 MW, and omitting N-1 security raises this to 532 MW, a 19.8% overestimate.

key_insights.text: Omitting N-1 branch-contingency security raises the estimated bus-level data center hosting capacity from 444 MW to 532 MW, a 19.8% overestimation.
Simpler models (DC-OPF and basic SCUC) further overestimate hosting capacity, indicating a trade-off between model complexity and estimation accuracy.
Grid-side modeling assumptions materially affect how much data center load a transmission bus can be assumed to host, which bears on interconnection planning.

title: Impact of Data Center Load on Co-Optimized Generation and Transmission Expansion Planning with Embedded Unit Commitment
author: Haoxiang Wan, Xingpeng Li, Jonghwan Kwon
summary: This arXiv paper models how a 500 MW data center load spread across four buses affects co-optimized transmission and generation expansion planning on a modified IEEE RTS-24 test system with ERCOT-calibrated renewable profiles. It reports a 61.6% rise in 15-year net present value of system cost and a 45.2% rise in average LMP, and finds the optimal plan shifts from a 230 kV transmission reinforcement to a new 400 MW combined-cycle gas turbine.

key_insights.text: A mixed-integer linear program with unit commitment embedded is used to co-optimize transmission and generation expansion over multiple years.
Existing renewables are near full utilization, so added data center demand is served almost entirely by incremental thermal generation.
Integrating the 500 MW load raises 15-year NPV of total system cost by 1,794 million USD, with operating cost making up 84.2% of the total.
Strategically sited generation can substitute for network reinforcement when serving data center load.

title: Service-Aware Hosting Capacity Assessment of Edge Data Centers with Workload Flexibility
author: Linhan Fang, Haoxiang Wan, Anurag Srivastava, Xingpeng Li
summary: The paper presents a hosting capacity assessment model for edge data centers with shiftable workload scheduling, accounting for fixed, service-driven, cooling, and shiftable demand. It embeds the resulting active and reactive loads in a distribution power flow model. On the IEEE 33-bus system, load shifting raises maximum bus-level hosting capacity by 4.46% for MEC data centers and 9.89% for AI data centers, with negligible gain for CDN cases.

key_insights.text: Fixed peak load representations can miss service-dependent demand, cooling-related demand, and delay-tolerant workloads when assessing hosting capacity.

Workload execution is optimized under arrival causality, maximum delay, and daily energy balance constraints, then embedded in a distribution power flow model checking feeder current and voltage limits.

Shifting workloads raises maximum bus-level hosting capacity by 4.46% for MEC data centers and 9.89% for AI data centers on the IEEE 33-bus system, while CDN shows negligible gain under the assumed cache windows.

title: A Power-Trajectory Framework for Data Center Participation in Day-Ahead Markets
author: Menghan Zhang, Caisheng Wang
summary: The paper proposes a power-trajectory framework in which data centers declare predictable aggregate demand evolution as continuous trajectories before day-ahead market clearing. It analyzes settlement effects of representation-induced power imbalances and supply-side compensation, illustrated with a 5-bus case and a modified IEEE RTS-GMLC case.

key_insights.text: Interval-based day-ahead energy blocks do not retain predictable intra-interval data center demand evolution, which can mismatch ramp-feasible generation trajectories.
Declared continuous demand trajectories are treated as exogenous inputs for constructing generation and price trajectories, with physical and economic temporal consistency established.
Trajectory-based settlement analysis quantifies the monetary magnitude of power imbalances and the supply-side compensation that may remain under temporally consistent clearing.

Includes a linear-programming carbon-aware compute scheduler and FastAPI serving for the forecasts.

key_insights.text: VA2 runs on onsite natural-gas turbines and is not connected to the grid; diesel generators serve as backup, and a turbine failure triggered the extended generator run.
Of Virginia's 197 data-center air permits, 189 are classified as minor, which requires neither public notice nor a public hearing.

key_insights.text: Records every GPU process from start to end, including peak GPU memory, runtime and how it ended (exit code, signal, OOM-killer likely, or stopped from dgxtop).

Requires the NVIDIA driver for GPU metrics; CPU, memory, disk and network monitoring work without it. Supports Linux x86_64 and aarch64 with glibc 2.34 or newer, and WSL 2, but not WSL 1, musl, macOS or Windows.
Installer verifies the release against SHA256SUMS and keeps the previous version, with a rollback option.

title: Stackelberg Game with Multi-Agent Transformer for ISRS-Aware Resource Re-optimization in Multi-Band Optical Networks
author: Jiaxin Liu, Rentao Gu, Miao Zhu, Zeguang Zou, Hui Li, Yuefeng Ji
summary: An arXiv paper proposes SG-MAT, a Stackelberg game with multi-agent transformer approach for resource re-optimization in multi-band optical networks affected by inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering. The authors report higher utilization gains and about 30% lower blocking ratio under moderate traffic loads than benchmarks, with comparable computational complexity. The work is motivated by connectivity between interconnected AI data centers.

key_insights.text: Multi-band transmission amplifies inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering, creating nonlinear coupling among services that complicates re-optimization.
SG-MAT uses a leader-follower structure where a MAT-based follower generates channel reallocations and the leader selects critical service subsets.
Simulation results report about 30% reduction in blocking ratio under moderate traffic loads, versus benchmarks.

title: Energy-Aware Agentic Orchestration for Multi-Site Service Deployment
author: Rodrigo Moreira, Alisson Chaves, Larissa F. Rodrigues Moreira, Tereza Carvalho, Tiago Barros, Daniel Corujo, Rui Aguiar, David Gomez-Barquero, Flávio de Oliveira Silva
summary: The paper presents an energy-aware agentic orchestration framework that treats LLM reasoning as a measurable part of the control loop for multi-site service deployment. It compares single-shot tool calling, ReAct, and plan-and-execute strategies on a Kubernetes testbed across two European data centers with per-pod energy attribution. It reports that reasoning strategy and intent complexity affect GPU energy during orchestration decisions, and that prefix caching reduced mean ReAct GPU energy by 29.4%.

key_insights.text: Prefix caching reduced mean ReAct GPU energy consumption by 29.4%.
ReAct and plan-and-execute produced executable tool calls across all evaluated intents but required multiple LLM inferences, while single-shot tool calling was less costly but non-actionable.

For the evaluated lightweight workload, infrastructure-energy changes within the one-second window were insufficient to offset the measured GPU decision energy, so reasoning overhead matters when assessing AI-native orchestration sustainability.

title: Dissecting the Carbon-SLO Tension in Geo-Distributed LLM Serving
author: Burak Topcu, Musa Cim, Zuhal Ozturk, Mahmut Taylan Kandemir
summary: The paper presents a latency-centric geo-distributed LLM inference simulator calibrated with hardware latency and power measurements, to study carbon savings under service-level objectives. It formulates greedy, ILP-based, iterative ILP, and facility MILP schedulers, reporting that the MILP option cuts carbon emissions by up to 60% versus round-robin with an average 3% SLO violation.

key_insights.text: Modeling queueing and continuous batching in inference engines is needed to capture latency dynamics when studying carbon-aware scheduling under strict SLOs.

A facility MILP scheduler that prices the energy of batched requests collectively gives the best carbon-SLO balance among the schedulers evaluated, with up to 60% carbon reduction versus round-robin and average 3% SLO violation.
Carbon savings grow with the spread of carbon intensity across datacenters and shrink as system load increases.

title: Large-Scale Data Center Integration in Power Systems: Uncertainty and Multi-Scale Variation
author: Le Xie, Dongjoo Kim, Qian Zhang, Grant Ruan, Paul L. Joskow
summary: This arXiv paper presents a framework for integrating large hyperscale AI data centers into power systems, linking reliability and affordability to load forecast uncertainty and multi-scale temporal variation. It analyzes measured GPU power traces from a public generative-AI workload dataset, which show tonal spectra and workload-dependent variance bands. The authors argue these loads warrant spectral description and affect reserves, ramping, voltage stability and harmonic interactions.

key_insights.text: Measured GPU power traces from AI workloads show strongly tonal spectra, with harmonic combs at the training-step cadence and sub-second periodicity in inference.
The dominant variance band shifts with workload type: seconds for training and offline inference, tens of seconds and longer for online inference.
AI data center loads affect reserve requirements, ramping products, voltage stability, ride-through performance and reliability and cost implications for grid planning.

The complex covers about 130,000 square meters with a planned 63 MW capacity and room for more than 3,800 racks at up to 15 kW each.

title: Sustainable Cloud-Fog-Edge Systems for Smart Buildings: Algorithmic Adaptation under Memory Constraints and Dynamic Orchestration Strategies
author: Mamadou Sow, Christophe Cerin
summary: The paper proposes an edge and fog computing architecture for smart buildings, framed around the building itself acting as a data center. It covers Arduino-based data acquisition, a KOptim orchestration framework for SLA management interoperable with FIWARE, and an adapted Generalized Hebbian Algorithm for PCA on low-power microcontrollers using sorted data buffers.

key_insights.text: A buffered iterative GHA-based PCA with sorting and preservation of extreme samples is reported to converge to results visually equivalent to full-memory processing on sensor data.
The sorting step adds O(W log W) temporal complexity to the learning strategy.
The paper frames data center electricity use, potentially reaching 3% by 2030, as motivation for shifting computation toward edge systems in buildings.

title: PCM: Programmable Congestion Management for Terabit RDMA NICs
author: Mikhail Khalilov, Timo Schneider, Tommaso Bonato, Siyuan Shen, Marcin Chrapek, Yehor Kozyr, Alberto Merino, Rip Sohan, Surendra Anubolu, Mohan Kalkunte et al.
summary: The paper introduces PCM, a programming model that separates portable datacenter congestion control and load balancing logic from RDMA NIC platform integration. It reports implementing eleven congestion control and load balancing algorithms and deploying them across an Ultra Ethernet simulator, CPU-based UCCL, and on-NIC offloads on NVIDIA ConnectX-8 and Microsoft 1P.

key_insights.text: PCM lets developers write event-driven congestion management handlers that can be debugged in simulation and reused on real RDMA hardware.
On ConnectX-8, PCM-Swift reaches processing capacity equivalent to one reaction per three 4 KiB packets at 800 Gbit/s while using one-fifth of the NIC's hardware threads.
In UCCL, PCM matches native Swift's 1.56 Tbit/s goodput with 64 KiB chunk-level control.
Operators currently must port each congestion policy to every platform they deploy, which PCM aims to reduce by separating portable logic from vendor backends.

title: Shai-Hulud worm makes jump to AI infrastructure with Tensorlake compromise

title: Capturing Electrical Windows Through Reconfigurable Optical Networks: Transfer-aware Scheduling of Multi-Region AI Data Centers
author: Xi Tong, Zijian Li, Xiaoyi Fan, Cong Zhang, Ershun Du, Qin Wang
summary: The paper proposes a transfer-aware scheduling framework for multi-region AI data centers that coordinates training placement, checkpoint transmission, and optical circuit switching to improve local renewable energy use and reduce grid purchase cost. In a five-AIDC benchmark, the method reduces real-time grid purchase cost by 12.50% and increases local renewable energy utilization by 2.724 percentage points relative to static optical operation. The authors report that optical circuit switching helps most when renewable-rich or low-price windows shift across sites and network bottlenecks delay checkpoint delivery.

key_insights.text: Transfer-aware scheduling accounts for checkpoint transfer delays that transfer-blind scheduling overlooks, which can otherwise overestimate migration benefits.
The framework verifies checkpoint delivery under shared-link capacity constraints and revises infeasible schedules using updated delay estimates.
In a five-AIDC benchmark, the method reduces real-time grid purchase cost by 12.50% versus static optical operation.

title: Execution-Feasible Dispatch of LLM Pre-training Loads for Renewable-Dominant AI Data Centers
author: Xi Tong, Ershun Du, Haiyang Jiang, Long Chen, Qin Wang
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a day-ahead dispatch framework that schedules LLM pre-training workloads in renewable-dominant AI data centers using checkpoint-domain workloads and feasible 3D-parallel GPU modes. In a case study of a 2048-GPU AI data center running two LLaMA pretraining tasks, the authors report a 20.02% operating cost reduction and renewable curtailment falling from 1.077 to 0.014 MWh compared with fixed continuous training.

key_insights.text: Checkpoint-aware 3D-parallel dispatch is presented as the source of practical grid-interactive flexibility, since checkpoint records alone do not create flexibility.
Scheduling LLM pre-training around renewable availability is reported to cut operating cost by 20.02% and sharply reduce renewable curtailment in the studied 2048-GPU case.

title: Virtual Transmission Lines from Data Center Workload Migration: Coordinated Multi-Year Transmission Expansion Planning
author: Mengxin Zhu, Qian Kai, Yadong Liu, Yingjie Yan, Haoyu Zhao
summary: This arXiv paper models geographic workload migration between data centers as a virtual transmission line that shifts nodal data-center demand without moving physical electricity. It proposes a mixed-integer linear programming model that co-optimizes multi-year transmission expansion and workload migration, evaluated on modified IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus systems.

key_insights.text: Coordinating virtual transmission lines from workload migration with physical transmission expansion reduces total system cost, unserved data-center load, and renewable curtailment.
VTL-aware planning requires one fewer candidate physical line than build-only planning, but VTL alone cannot meet system demand.
VTL provides the greatest value when transfer capacity is tight, construction costs are high, load growth is rapid, and data-center flexibility is greater.

title: Democratizing MoE inference on commodity GPUs with CoMoE
author: Ruwen Fan, Yuezhi Zu, Minhui Xie, Junru Li, Qingda Hu, Xinjun, Yang, Jiwu Shu, Youyou Lu
summary: The arXiv paper presents CoMoE, an MoE inference system for consumer GPUs that uses host-centric routing to reduce inter-GPU communication over PCIe without P2P support. The authors report up to 1.46x throughput improvement on RTX 5090 GPUs, approaching NVLink-capable A800 performance at 23.4% of the hardware cost.

key_insights.text: Host-backed token multicast writes shared tokens to the host once, eliminating redundant outbound transmission for token dispatch.
Fine-grained token-level aggregation using host staging buffers replaces global synchronization and mitigates straggler effects during token combine.
The approach targets lower-cost MoE inference deployment, reporting performance near NVLink-capable A800 GPUs at 23.4% of hardware cost.

title: Trajectory Sensitivity-Based Dynamic Assessment of an AI Data Center Under Contingencies
author: Arnav Bagga, Saskia A. Putri, Abhishek Banerjee, Xiaofan Wu
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a trajectory sensitivity-based framework for assessing the dynamic response of a self-contained AI data center supplied by a 2 kV DC microgrid. The method models data-hall load profiles, a VSC, BESS units, supercapacitors, and synchronous sources, and is validated against full nonlinear simulations with ±15% parameter perturbations. The authors report reducing evaluation time from seconds to milliseconds.

key_insights.text: Trajectory sensitivity is used to estimate system trajectories under simultaneous parameter perturbations, avoiding repeated full nonlinear time-domain solutions.
The AI data center microgrid includes a voltage source converter, battery energy storage, supercapacitors, and synchronous-generation-side sources on a 2 kV DC microgrid with a grid-tied interface.
The reported reduction from seconds to milliseconds positions the approach as a scalable screening tool for AI data center dynamics.

title: AI Data Centers Meet Electrical Grids: A Review of Power Challenges and Coordinated Solutions
author: Mariam Mughees, Yuzhuo Li, Yize Chen, Yunwei Ryan Li
summary: This review examines how AI data centers affect power system stability, renewable integration, and low-carbon planning, tracing the power-delivery chain from accelerators and rack converters through UPS, storage, and microgrids to the transmission interconnection point. It covers mitigation strategies across device, rack, facility, and grid levels, and identifies research needs such as dynamic load models and carbon-aware scheduling.

key_insights.text: AI workloads create large power-electronic loads whose grid effects depend on location, temporal variability, and controllability, so annual electricity consumption alone is insufficient.
Facility responses such as UPS and rack converters can amplify grid disturbances, while programmable workloads and controllable converters offer demand flexibility.
Lower energy per token does not necessarily reduce peak demand, electrical disturbances, or carbon emissions.

title: OrigaMIG: MIG-Aware VM Placement with a Neighborhood-Restricted BILP and Live Migration
author: Ahmad Siavashi, Mahmoud Momtazpour
summary: The paper models MIG-aware VM placement on GPU-equipped cloud data centers as a binary integer linear programming problem aimed at request acceptance, consolidation, and reduced migration. It proposes OrigaMIG, which uses a greedy placement rule and invokes a neighborhood-restricted solver with live migrations, and reports simulation results against default and state-of-the-art policies on 256 A100 and A30 GPUs.

key_insights.text: MIG placement rules cause fragmentation and suboptimal allocation, which OrigaMIG addresses by calling the BILP solver only when a request cannot be placed or GPUs become fragmented.
The solver runs on a small neighborhood of physical machines while the rest of the data center stays fixed, with solutions executed as live migrations.
In simulation on 256 A100 and A30 GPUs in 128 PMs, the approach keeps fewer PMs active and uses the least energy per admitted GPU-hour at every load tested.

title: Unlocking AI Data Center Interconnection Capacity Through Coordinated Grid and Data Center Flexibility
author: Rida Fatima, Xingpeng Li
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a day-ahead optimization framework that coordinates grid-side flexibility (conservation voltage reduction and network reconfiguration) with data center workload shifting and UPS storage to increase feasible AI data center IT capacity at a constrained interconnection bus. Simulations on a 116-bus model derived from the IEEE 123-node feeder report coordinated operation raising feasible IT capacity from about 10.5-10.6 MW to 15.3-16.0 MW.

key_insights.text: Grid-side flexibility, driven almost entirely by network reconfiguration, increases feasible IT capacity by about 42.5-45.0% at the constrained bus-60 connection point, while data center flexibility alone provides about 2.1-5.4% gains.

Coordinated operation of grid and data center flexibility raises feasible IT capacity from about 10.5-10.6 MW to 15.3-16.0 MW, with the Inference result limited by the adopted UPS reserve requirement.
Coordinating flexibility on both sides of the interconnection can help AI data centers connect despite distribution network headroom limits that would otherwise delay interconnection.

technologies: mixed integer second order cone programming

title: arkady-emelyanov/ai-lab
author: arkady-emelyanov

It runs real Slurm or Kubernetes, PyTorch and NCCL against emulated GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch partitions, Redfish BMCs and InfiniBand.

key_insights.text: Emulates GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch, Redfish BMC and InfiniBand behavior so cluster software can be tested without physical GB200 hardware.
Lets teams validate GPU cluster software and infrastructure workflows on a single machine before deploying on production hardware.

key_insights.text: The project reproduces HPCC at the 320-host scale used in the original paper using a packet-level simulator.
The simulator is deterministic and written in Rust, and it implements HPCC, DCQCN, DCTCP and TIMELY congestion control schemes.
Results are cross-checked against the authors' ns-3 simulator.

title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration for Constrained Multi-Objective Container Placement
author: Suvarthi Sarkar, Abhishek Hazra, Akshat Mittal, Aryabartta Sahu
summary: The paper proposes an LLM-driven multi-agent framework for container placement in data centers that balances power consumption against affinity preferences under resource and anti-affinity constraints. Four agents operate in a ReAct loop, with a rearrangement phase refining placements. Experiments on the Google Cluster Trace with 100 applications and 25 machines report 8.36% lower power use and 39.30% higher affinity than a power-greedy baseline, and ablations show each component contributes.

key_insights.text: Agents reason over deterministic, feasibility-filtered candidate tables, so every proposed action satisfies hard capacity and anti-affinity constraints.
Ablation studies show removing any single component (multi-round debate, Tolerance-Gated Arbitration, or Monotone Improvement Rule) degrades both power consumption and affinity.
Reported results show 8.36% less power and 39.30% higher affinity than a power-greedy baseline on a 100-application, 25-machine configuration.
