title: Parallel Architectures For Priority Scheduling In Programmable Data Plane Switches
author: Nikhil Shinde, Krishna M. Sivalingam, Gauravdeep Shami
summary: The paper proposes two packet queuing architectures, P3PO and PPQA, for programmable data plane switches. Both split a large global priority queue into smaller parallel priority queues to scale accurate packet scheduling to speeds of 100 Gbps and beyond. The architectures are evaluated in the NetBench simulator using Web-search and Data-mining datacenter workloads.

key_insights.text: Accurate PIFO-based priority scheduling is limited at high network speeds by the requirement for line-rate packet sorting.
P3PO uses cascading priority queues with priority-based bounds to insert packets into the earliest queue that maintains ordering.
PPQA distributes packets across independent priority queues by occupancy, using a demultiplexer for balanced queuing and a multiplexer to select the highest-priority packet at dequeue.
Approximate schedulers such as SP-PIFO, AIFO and RIFO introduce priority inversions that degrade latency, fairness and flow completion times.

title: Sparse Distributed Fiber Optic Sensor Placement in Metropolitan and Datacenter Elastic Optical Networks
author: Sleman Mouammar, Ítalo B. Brasileiro, André Drummond
summary: This arXiv paper studies how the number and placement of distributed fiber optical sensing devices in all-optical metropolitan and data center elastic optical networks can mitigate failures. It evaluates placement heuristics and prediction windows using blocking rate, affected circuits, and downtime, and reports that 5% to 25% link coverage can yield large gains.

key_insights.text: The Greedy Shortest Path Coverage heuristic substantially reduces the number of circuits affected by failures when DFOS devices cover only 5% of links.
Prediction windows of 15 ms (metropolitan) and 7.5 ms (data center) are reported as sufficient for just-in-time restoration at 5% coverage.
25% sensing coverage performs comparably to full coverage, suggesting significant cost reduction opportunities.

title: How suboptimal is my stochastic network controller allowed to be? Completion certificates with application to power grids hosting AI data centers
author: Michael Chertkov
summary: The paper frames grid control for power systems hosting AI data centers as a stochastic control problem and bounds how far a deployed controller is from optimal. It builds lower bounds from path-integral control subsolutions and upper bounds from simulation. On the IEEE 118-bus system after a severe load loss, a simple generator controller is certified within 2.8% of optimal under homogeneous forcing, and repricing control authority reduces a 39% heterogeneous-forcing gap to 1.2%.

key_insights.text: Lower bounds come from HJB subsolutions built by completing the control geometry, and simulation gives the upper bound, so their gap certifies permissible suboptimality.
On the IEEE 118-bus system after a severe load loss, a simple generator controller is certified within 2.8% of optimal under homogeneous forcing.
Under heterogeneous forcing, the gap is 39% with uniform control prices and 1.2% after repricing the same total authority, before any hardware is added.

title: New evidence on data center employment effects
author: gradus_ad
summary: A Brookings brief summarizes the paper 'Data Centers and Local Labor Markets' by Dany Bahar and Greg Wright, which compares U.S. counties with built data centers to counties with announced-but-canceled projects. The brief reports that counties receiving a first large data center see data processing and telecommunications employment rise, with wages unchanged and modest home price increases. The piece also covers the policy debate over data center moratoriums, tax incentives, and electricity costs.

key_insights.text: Labor markets receiving their first large data center see data processing employment rise 56% over the first decade of operations, and telecommunications rise 43%.
Wages were unchanged and home prices rose 2%-5%, according to the brief.
Virginia's data-center sales-tax exemption cost an estimated $1.6 billion in fiscal year 2025, which the brief notes may subsidize investments that would have happened anyway.
The study uses about 1,500 U.S. data center facilities, 52 announced-but-canceled projects, and county-level BLS data from 2003-2024.

title: Generation and Transmission Expansion Planning with BESS-Based Virtual Transmission Lines
author: Qiushi Wang, Xingpeng Li
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a long-term generation and transmission expansion planning model that adds a virtual transmission line built from a pair of battery storage systems, coordinated so they do not charge or discharge simultaneously. It is evaluated on a revised IEEE 24-bus system and reports a 12.3% reduction in weighted total congestion for a 0.3% increase in planning cost. The motivation mentions renewable growth and integrated data centers in deregulated power markets.

key_insights.text: Coordinating two BESS units so they do not charge or discharge simultaneously provides congestion relief without an explicit congestion cost in the objective.
Virtual transmission lines built from storage may offer congestion mitigation as a complement to standalone BESS at modest added planning cost.

title: Nvidia debuted the Open Agent Safety Platform

A policy prover uses formal verification to check whether policies stay within an allowed access boundary and whether proposed network rules add risk.
Enterprise IT and security teams can enable agent development without giving every agent broad access to hosts, networks, credentials, or model endpoints.

title: MANTA: Machine Learning Augmented Tiering Advisor
author: Johannes Freischuetz, Kiet Pham, Sujay Yadalam, Konstantinos Kanellis, Michael Swift, Shivaram Venkataraman
summary: An arXiv paper introduces MANTA, a machine-learning-augmented memory tiering advisor that predicts page usefulness to place data between fast DRAM and slower tiers such as CXL-attached memory. The paper also presents ChOMP, an offline optimizer and trace-driven simulator used as a reference for online policies, and reports geometric-mean speedups over ARMS on emulated CXL and Optane workloads.

key_insights.text: Heuristic memory tiering policies can lag behind changing hot sets in phased or bursty workloads.
MANTA predicts future page usefulness from runtime access features and integrates a lightweight learned model into ARMS.
Reported speedups over ARMS are 1.12x and 1.08x on emulated CXL at 4 GB fast memory on Linux 6.2 and 6.18, and 1.69x across six Optane workloads.

title: Aging-Aware Online Distributed Scheduling for Lifecycle Carbon Reduction in Geo-Distributed Data Centers
author: Junyu Lin, Wenjie Liu, Shunbo Lei, Wentian Lu, Jianhui Wang, Junhong Liu
summary: An arXiv paper proposes a lifecycle carbon modeling framework for geo-distributed data centers that adds server aging and thermal-stress-driven replacement emissions to operational carbon. It presents an online, privacy-preserving distributed scheduling method using a Lyapunov framework and ZSP-ADMM, reporting up to 13.0% lower carbon emissions and 12.6% lower operational costs versus benchmarks.

key_insights.text: Workload-induced thermal stress accelerates nonlinear hardware degradation, which shortens server life and raises embodied carbon via more frequent replacements.
A utilization-dependent exponential aging model is combined with workload scheduling to estimate long-term carbon costs from server degradation.

The method uses an enhanced Lyapunov framework with time-varying queue shifting and a zero-sum perturbation-based ADMM to coordinate data centers online while protecting exchanged workload information.
Simulation results report up to 13.0% lower carbon emissions and 12.6% lower operational costs compared with benchmarks.

title: FissionReady: Joint Workload and Power Scheduling for Data Centers Powered by Small Modular Reactors
author: Raghavendra Kanakagiri, Rohan Basu Roy, Yankai Jiang, Pranathi Wuppuluru, Devesh Tiwari
summary: The paper proposes FissionReady, a data center scheduler for small modular reactor (SMR) powered sites that tracks per-module fuel age, xenon state and flexibility to coordinate load-following, batch deferral and grid purchasing. The authors report zero involuntary shutdowns and zero batch deadline misses, with roughly one-third less water use and about half the grid cost compared with a same-sized base configuration.

key_insights.text: FissionReady tracks each SMR module's fuel age, xenon state and remaining flexibility to set per-module operating envelopes.
A two-timescale optimization coordinates load-following, batch deferral and grid purchasing.
Reported results include roughly half the grid cost and roughly one-third less water consumption versus a same-sized base configuration.

title: Grid Demand Flexibility Assessment of AI Data Centers via Batch Workload Temporal Shifting
author: Suntao Su, Liang Du, Shengyi Wang
summary: An arXiv paper proposes a framework for assessing how much grid-compatible demand flexibility AI data centers can offer by temporally shifting batch workloads. The method maps fine-resolution CPU, GPU and memory usage into power-system time intervals and couples a workload scheduling model with a utilization-dependent server power model. Numerical results using real GPU cluster traces are reported for peak shaving and sustained power reduction metrics.

key_insights.text: Averaging-based processing maps fine-resolution CPU, GPU and memory usage into time intervals compatible with power system operation.
Batch workload temporal shifting is evaluated with peak demand shaving and maximum duration of sustained power reduction as flexibility metrics.
Workload shifting may provide grid-compatible demand flexibility for AI data centers with limited disruption to computing workloads.

title: Joint Effects of GPU Server Topology, Parallelism, and Congestion Control on MoE Inference: A Controlled Simulation Study
author: Kaikai Yuan, Rui Xi, Yu Liu
summary: An arXiv simulation study uses ASTRA-sim with an NS-3 backend to evaluate how GPU server topology, tensor and expert parallelism, collective algorithms, and congestion control affect completion time for MoE inference across 32 GPU ranks. Across 768 deterministic simulations, exposed communication accounts for most completion time, and the authors conclude these factors jointly determine performance.

key_insights.text: Exposed communication accounts for 89.9% to 95.8% of mean completion time in the feedback-enabled subset per model.
TP16EP2 requires 3.68 to 4.35 times the mean completion time of TP2EP16.
With fixed rank mapping, Double Binary Tree incurs 28.3% to 83.2% more time than Ring, and RoCE with DCQCN is 23.8% to 35.7% slower than RoCE HPCC.
Topology benefits are conditional: additional GPUs or NICs help only when rank mapping balances traffic across injection paths.

key_insights.text: Power flow, economic dispatch, market clearing, and device dynamics are rewritten as JAX computation graphs so the training and evaluation loop runs entirely on the GPU.
One of the five benchmark tasks models a data center microgrid, alongside generation, transmission, distribution, and distributed energy resources tasks.
The open-source benchmark is intended to make large-scale evaluation of RL controllers for power system operation practical.

title: Heddle: Learning Structural Templates for Parallelism Planning on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters
author: Taeyoon Kim, Yonguk Song, Seoyeong Choy, Hexiao Duan, Dong Li, Seo Jin Park, Myeongjae Jeon
summary: Heddle is a learning-based parallelism planner for training large machine learning models on heterogeneous GPU clusters. It reduces planning to searching over pipeline structural templates learned offline across cluster configurations.

key_insights.text: Planning is reduced to a search over pipeline structures, with remaining plan details derived by rule or from a small candidate set once structure is fixed.
The planner is evaluated against five existing planners across clusters with varying GPU types and node sizes, with throughput gains of up to 84.5% on dense models and 4.6x on MoE models.

title: Integrated Thermal and Power Management for Wave-Powered Subsea Data Centers via Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
author: Wanqun Yang, Jun Chen
summary: This arXiv paper presents an integrated model and nonlinear model predictive control framework that coordinates thermal management, flexible workload scheduling, wave-power use, and battery operation in a wave-powered subsea data center. The framework is evaluated with closed-loop simulations using job-level workloads from the MIT Supercloud dataset, along with parametric, Monte Carlo, and distance-correlation analyses. The authors report that battery and wave-generation capacity mainly affect battery availability and flexible-workload queueing.

key_insights.text: A nonlinear model predictive controller jointly optimizes the flexible workload power budget and the cooling command under thermal, battery, and workload constraints.
Thermal behavior is modeled with a three-node lumped model covering IT equipment, recirculating nitrogen, and the pressure hull, with surrounding seawater as the thermal boundary.
Excessive renewable generation capacity may increase energy curtailment, according to the parametric studies.
Flexible-job delay is relatively insensitive to the investigated parameters, while terminal battery state-of-charge depends mainly on battery energy capacity and wave generation capacity.

title: Grid-Forming E-STATCOMs for Stable Integration of Large-Scale Data Centers: Modeling and Control
author: Prabhat Ranjan Bana, Novan Zakkia, Jean-Philippe Hasler, Christer Danielsson
summary: This arXiv paper studies grid-forming Enhanced STATCOMs for integrating large AI data centers into weak, low-inertia grids. It presents a power-admittance linear modelling framework validated with EMT simulations, reporting fast damped responses to abrupt load changes and mitigation of low-frequency oscillations.

key_insights.text: Grid-forming E-STATCOMs are proposed to provide fast, well-damped response to abrupt AI data center load changes in weak grids.
A power-admittance-based linear model, validated by EMT simulations, is used to capture system interactions and network resonances.
The paper frames the approach as a way to meet grid codes and AIDC interconnection requirements with less reliance on EMT studies.

Coolant flow is regulated with a PID controller, and pump power is scaled cubically.
The simulation is driven by compute telemetry inputs.

title: Job Class Thermal Intent Aware Liquid Cooling Allocation for AI Data Centers
author: Krishna Chaitanya Sunkara
summary: An arXiv paper proposes Job-Class Thermal Intent (JCTI), which passes job class information from the scheduler to the liquid cooling controller so coolant can be staged before heat rises. Reported Monte Carlo trials over 120 paired runs show 56.4% fewer thermal violations and 60.2% less cumulative overshoot compared with a PI control loop. The authors also argue the approach can reduce sudden grid demand swings for gigawatt-scale AI data centers.

key_insights.text: Cooling loops typically react only after a temperature sensor detects a rise, which can take 30 to 50 seconds; JCTI uses scheduler knowledge of incoming jobs to pre-stage coolant.
Thermal signatures per job class were derived from MLPerf GPU power traces, and arrival patterns were tuned against Alibaba cluster data.
Reported results show 56.4% fewer thermal violations and 60.2% less cumulative overshoot than a straight PI loop across 120 paired Monte Carlo trials.
The authors suggest thermally aware scheduling could smooth power swings and improve load prediction on the grid side.

title: Beyond the Last Truffula Tree: SustainAI - A Water-Aware, Closed-Loop Framework for Environmentally Accountable AI
author: Farnaz Farid, Tashfia Towkee, Sania Nasreen, Sami bin Azad

In an evaluation with Small Language Models across geographically distributed data centers, per-inference water footprint varied about 11-fold, and a substantial share of water went to incorrect outputs.

key_insights.text: Per-inference water footprint varied roughly 11-fold across geographically distributed data centers, from 0.0477 mL to 0.5360 mL.
A water-aware routing algorithm accounts for regional water stress when distributing inference workloads.
Across 1,335 runs, about 399 mL of water produced only 240 correct outputs, indicating resources spent on inaccurate responses.

title: So You Want to Build Your Own Data Center

key_insights.text: Railway chose cage colocation over greenfield buildout or rack colocation, and power, which drives cooling costs, was the largest expense.
Server and CPU selection was driven mainly by power density, and each rack needs two fully independent power feeds designed to survive loss of one.

title: When Gigawatts of Computational Load Disappear: Cycle-Space Certificates for Grid Synchronization and Transient Stability
author: Michael Chertkov
summary: This arXiv paper presents a cycle-space certificate framework for analyzing synchronization and transient stability of power grids under large, sudden data center load disconnections. It evaluates the approach on MATPOWER benchmarks and a stylized 2.7-GW 39-bus event.

key_insights.text: The exact strict-cohesion static test admits 16.2% more loading than the sufficient Dörfler–Chertkov–Bullo screen on the 118-bus case.
In a stylized 2.7-GW 39-bus event, transient margin can change by about a factor of two depending on where balancing power is supplied, even when final operating points are statically feasible.
Routine transmission disturbances can cause several gigawatts of data center demand to disconnect or transfer to backup nearly simultaneously, motivating grid stability analysis.

title: Forced Oscillations in Power Systems Induced by Data Centers Hosting AI Workloads
author: Jovan Krajacic, Georgia Pierrou, Maitraya Desai, Gabriela Hug, Gustavo Valverde
summary: This arXiv paper analyzes how power swings from large data centers running AI workloads can excite poorly damped modes and cause forced oscillations in power systems. It uses transfer-function analysis to identify critical grid locations and characterizes instability mechanisms and the interaction of two oscillating data centers.

key_insights.text: Power swings from large AI-workload data centers can excite poorly damped power system modes, leading to forced oscillations that may cause flicker, equipment disconnection, or blackouts.

Instabilities are classified as saddle-node bifurcations of the forced periodic response and impasse-surface encounters, analyzed with Floquet multipliers and the minimum singular value of the algebraic Jacobian.
The findings can help system operators define regulations on maximum load fluctuations permitted for data center facilities at specific grid locations.

title: EMA: Elastic and Performance Transparent Memory Across GPUs
author: Yi Xu, Tian Xia, Ion Stoica
summary: EMA is an arXiv research paper presenting a memory sharing system that lets GPUs within a multi-GPU server borrow and reclaim memory from each other to form an elastic pool. The paper claims prefetching makes remote memory performance indistinguishable from local memory, and reports up to 52% higher individual user throughput and 96% of the throughput of a system with 2X capacity.

key_insights.text: EMA lets GPUs within a server borrow and reclaim memory from each other, addressing imbalanced memory demand such as LLM inference workloads.
Prefetching is used to hide remote access costs so borrowers see remote and local memory as performance-equivalent.
Reported evaluation shows up to 52% higher individual user throughput and 96% of the throughput of a system provisioned with 2X capacity.

The article links the project to US-Armenia relations, Nvidia export licensing, and the Armenia-Azerbaijan peace process.

key_insights.text: Firebird's Armenian data center will reach 300 MW by the end of next year, with about one fifth of capacity for domestic use and the remainder allocated to foreign companies.
The facility will be equipped with more than 70,000 cutting-edge chips and is described as becoming the region's largest computing cluster.
Nvidia export licences are reported as part of US diplomatic negotiations linked to the Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement.

title: Toki: Profiling HBM Performance on FPGA Systems with RISC-V Soft Cores and PCIe Host DMA Traffic
author: Andrea Galimberti, Andrea Motta, Gianni Antichi, Davide Zoni
summary: Toki is an open-source hardware-software framework for profiling HBM performance on FPGA accelerator cards, combining workloads on RISC-V soft cores with memory traffic injected from the host over PCIe DMA. The paper reports experiments on an AMD Alveo U55C card with up to 60 RISC-V cores and HBM2 memory, using real applications and microbenchmarks.

key_insights.text: Profiling jointly considers RISC-V soft-core workload execution and host memory traffic injected via PCIe DMA, which synthetic traffic generators alone cannot capture.
Experiments on an AMD Alveo U55C card with up to 60 RISC-V cores measure the effects of core organization, memory access patterns, data locality, and memory controller contention on HBM performance.

title: Privacy-Preserving Coordinated Operation of Power Grids and AI Data Centers: A Checkpoint-Aware Three-Phase Scheme
author: Ziang Liu, Ruizhang Yang, Xin Cui, Francis Yunhe Hou
summary: The paper proposes a hierarchical, privacy-preserving three-phase scheme for coordinating power grid operation with AI data centers. It uses a certified inner approximation of the AI data center security region, workload allocation with checkpoint alerts, and a checkpoint-aware two-stage robust optimal power flow. Numerical studies use a modified IEEE 14-bus system and a modified NYISO system.

key_insights.text: AI data centers can adjust workloads through dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, and periodic checkpointing can cause abrupt power drops and rebounds that affect operating reserves and congestion risk.
The scheme exchanges only compact interface information between grid and AI data center operators, aiming to preserve privacy and avoid frequent iterative communication.
Grid and AI data center operators are generally unwilling to share proprietary data and decision-making authority, which motivates the privacy-preserving design.

title: Nvidia chip-use emissions match that of a Russian state coal producer: report
author: devonnull
summary: A report by environmental and civil society groups estimates that operating Nvidia chips sold since 2022 could have produced 4 to 21 million tonnes of CO2 in 2025, depending on the electricity used. The report also says Nvidia's Scope 3 supply chain emissions rose about 725% since 2020, from roughly 1.3 to 10.7 million tonnes CO2e, and challenges Nvidia's claims about AI's net climate benefit and demand response.

key_insights.text: Nvidia's supply chain emissions rose mainly from upstream emissions of producing components, materials and manufacturing services for its GPUs and AI systems.
Estimated emissions from operating Nvidia chips depend on assumed utilisation and grid emissions factors, and Nvidia does not currently disclose emissions from the use of sold products.
The report argues that efficiency gains may not offset overall impact when demand for computing power is rising rapidly, and questions Nvidia's demand response claims for grid support.

title: Data center cooling choices shift water impacts across the grid: An integrated water-energy model for sustainable data center development
author: Garrett Alston, Nancy Love, Rabab Haider
summary: An arXiv paper presents an integrated water-energy model linking data center cooling and electricity demand to hourly economic dispatch and monthly subbasin water depletion. Applied to proposed developments in Michigan, it finds air-cooled facilities halve total water use versus evaporative cooling but raise indirect water consumption by one-third through higher electricity demand. The authors argue data center water and energy impacts must be assessed together.

key_insights.text: Air-cooled data centers halve total water consumption relative to evaporative cooling but increase electricity demand, raising indirect water consumption by one-third.
Attributing indirect water use to generators and hydrologic regions, rather than the facility location, reveals depletion beyond data center sites.

title: RoutingBench: Can Agentic Routing Analysis Scale to Production Datacenter Networks?

title: Communication Delay Robust Control of BESS for AI Training Load Smoothing
author: Xue Lyu, Wei Du, Sheik Mohammad Mohiuddin, Brett A. Ross
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a hybrid battery energy storage system control strategy that combines droop-based grid-forming control with load-current-based compensation to smooth rapid power fluctuations from AI training loads at the data center point of common coupling. It models communication delay between load measurements and the BESS controller, and adds a predictor-based compensation method to reduce delay-induced degradation. The authors report validation through electromagnetic transient simulations across different grid strengths and time-varying delays.

key_insights.text: AI training loads have rapid power fluctuations because power demand differs between computational and communication phases, creating challenging ramp rates at the data center point of common coupling.
A predictor-based compensation method is added to the BESS control structure to mitigate degradation caused by communication delay.
The hybrid control uses grid-forming droop control for long-term power exchange and load-following compensation for short-term AI workload fluctuations.
Battery energy storage in data centers is presented as a mitigation option for AI training load fluctuations.

title: Improved Droop Control in DC Microgrids via Voltage-Locked Loop Synchronization

It separates control into a virtual DC machine for transient response and a virtual current source for steady-state power sharing, and validates the approach in an experimental microgrid setup. The abstract names fast-varying loads in AI datacenters as a motivating application.

key_insights.text: Conventional droop control suffers from poor transient performance, causing voltage dips and overshoots under fast-varying loads such as AI datacenters.
The proposed scheme splits control between a virtual DC machine that handles transient damping and a virtual current source that handles slow steady-state power balance.
The method was validated in an experimental microgrid setup, not only in simulation.

key_insights.text: COMET is a fully hardware-offloaded packet-arrival tracking design implemented on an FPGA-based NIC for multi-path RDMA over lossy WANs.
COMET sustains line rate at 400 Gbps and decouples on-chip memory footprint from link bandwidth-delay product.
The cache-based architecture supports six times more concurrent connections than state-of-the-art SoC-based designs.
Extending RDMA across WANs is presented as necessary for interconnecting multiple datacenters into a single AI factory.

The framework aims to give grid operators actionable dynamic specifications for large data center loads and to inform load-shaping mechanisms.

title: Towards Training Private LLMs: Exploring Fine-Tuning Language Models on Apple Silicon with RDMA over Thunderbolt

title: The Global Data Center Boom Is a Gift to Spies

Shared infrastructure such as virtualization software, GPUs, and management and cooling systems carries vulnerabilities that can let one tenant access another's environment.
Data center vacancies are near zero for the third year in a row, so tenants take whatever space is available, and landlords rarely disclose who else occupies the floor.
Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent are investing billions in new data centers across Southeast Asia, where American firms are also seeking capacity.

title: Bio-inspired Learning and Decision-Making with Probabilistic In-Memory Computing Hardware: Part 2
author: Thomas Dalgaty, Eiji Kawasaki, Miguel de Prado, Tommaso Salvatori, Germain Haugou, Eric Flamand
summary: This arXiv report extends earlier work on an energy-based model for learning and decision-making under uncertainty, which uses stochastic Langevin dynamics. key_insights.text: Massively parallel models with low arithmetic intensity are argued to be mismatched with GPUs that depend on HBM interfaces, causing sequential execution constraints.
Eliminating the HBM interface and computing directly within on-chip memory is presented as the route to much faster execution of the energy-based model.

title: Phase-Decoupled, Model-Calibrated Power Control for Disaggregated LLM Serving

key_insights.text: Optimal GPU power setting depends on the deployed model, quantization, engine and hardware combination rather than on GPU class alone.
Decode lanes draw flat, memory-bound power, so a power cap binds continuously and avoids the reactive-overshoot weakness cited for capping.
Reported energy savings are specific to MoE models; a dense model recovers roughly 5x less, so the claims are scoped to MoE serving.

Using 8 selected chiplets, the framework reports 48.5% energy and 97.8% energy-delay-cost product reductions versus homogeneous accelerators.

title: Spatial LLM Workload Shifting Needs Foresight: Model Commitment for AI Data Center Operation under Power Grid Constraints

summary: The paper proposes model commitment (MC), a mixed-integer linear programming framework that jointly schedules LLM model deployment and cross-site request routing for AI data centers facing power supply constraints. title: QPS-ToR: A Parallel Iterative Switching Algorithm for Reconfigurable Optical Datacenter Switching
author: Dongzhao Song, Qianru Yu, Jun Xu
summary: The paper proposes QPS-ToR, a scheduling algorithm for reconfigurable optical data center networks that replaces NegotiaToR's single-iteration iSLIP engine with a sliding-window QPS scheduler. The authors report up to 36% higher throughput and 82% lower flow completion time versus NegotiaToR in flow-level simulations with 128 ToRs, and better results than RotorNet on the parallel network topology.

key_insights.text: NegotiaToR's single-iteration iSLIP scheduler limits throughput to around 60%, and it gives all source-destination pairs equal priority regardless of queue length.
QPS-ToR reduces the scheduling cycle from three-step Request-Grant-Accept to two-step Request-Grant with a sliding window mechanism, reaching around 90% throughput in one low-complexity iteration.
Simulated results show up to 36% higher throughput and 82% lower flow completion time than NegotiaToR under realistic datacenter workloads.

title: Unifying Power Flow and Electromagnetic Transient Modeling
author: Tina Gao, Aayushya Agarwala, Timothy McNamara, Lawrence Pileggi
summary: An arXiv paper introduces SALT, a steady-state grid analysis framework that uses full-physics electromagnetic transient (EMT) device models instead of simplified power flow models. The authors report EMT-level steady-state accuracy with a 1x10^6 speedup and find that power flow analyses miss contingency violations that SALT captures.

key_insights.text: Power flow simplified device models are inconsistent with EMT models, so steady-state solutions do not match the time-to-infinity EMT response.
SALT builds algebraic frequency-domain representations of state-space power device models and reports a 1x10^6 speedup over EMT with steady-state accuracy.
Inverter-based resources and data centers reduce inertia and operating reserves, so power flow approximations risk missing grid security violations.

title: Beyond Scalar Flexibility: From Eligible AI Workloads to Dependable Load Relief
author: Meiyi Li
summary: The paper reconstructs hourly power observations from a 185-day trace of 155,410 GPUs to derive a workload-based flexibility envelope for data center load relief. It finds that eligible curtailment is a small share of load and that firmness declines with event duration, while aggregating clusters and scheduler deferral add limited gains. The authors argue that duration, reliability, portfolio and realizability terms should replace fixed flexibility percentages in interconnection and demand-response contracts.

key_insights.text: Immediate eligible curtailment averages 3.55 MW, about 12.1% of workload power and 6.35% of median facility power.
A mean-calibrated scalar overstates relief by 17%, 25%, and 47% across the one-hour, four-hour, and 24-hour cases.
Replacing fixed flexibility percentages with duration and reliability terms could be written into interconnection and demand-response contracts.
Aggregating 13 clusters raises four-hour firmness from 0.38 to 0.66, but cross-cluster covariance limits the gain.

title: A Wavelength Borrowing Architecture for Optical Data Center Networks - Extended Version

summary: This arXiv paper proposes a spine-leaf all-optical data center network architecture in which wavelengths unused or lightly loaded at one leaf can be borrowed by leaves with higher demand. A tunable borrowing degree B controls reconfigurability, and the paper reports performance near that of a fully reconfigurable design at well below maximum B. The fabric uses AWGs, AWGRs, colorless OXCs and combiners, and is suited to pod-level traffic that varies over tens of minutes or longer.

key_insights.text: A tunable borrowing degree B sets wavelength reconfigurability from none to full, and near-full performance is reached well below the maximum B.
Two-hop detouring combined with wavelength borrowing controls wavelength load while limiting detoured traffic.
The architecture avoids the complexity of a fully reconfigurable optical solution, using mature data-center-grade components.

title: Hosting Capacity Assessment of Data Centers with Voltage Ride-Through Capability in Power Systems
author: Pengyu Ren, Wei Sun, Fei Teng
summary: The paper presents a co-planning framework that couples transmission-level fault simulation with an internal data center ride-through model to assess data center hosting capacity under voltage disturbances. A case study on the IEEE 118-bus system finds that internal voltage ride-through capability can be a binding interconnection constraint, and that grid-forming operation gives greater ride-through margin than grid-following under the same faults.

key_insights.text: Internal voltage ride-through capability, including UPS converter headroom, can be a binding constraint on data center interconnection, and steady-state planning alone can overestimate feasible capacity.
In the reduced-order models studied, grid-forming mode provides greater ride-through margin than current-limited grid-following mode under the same network faults.
VRT constraints can change both total data center hosting capacity and how that capacity is allocated across candidate interconnection buses.

title: Performance Characterization of SPEC CPU 2026 on AMD EPYC 9755 Processor
author: Kunal Kashyap, Rajiv Ramanathan, Shayantika Bhattacharya
summary: This arXiv paper presents a microarchitecture-level performance characterization of SPEC CPU 2026 on AMD EPYC 9755 processors based on Zen 5. It analyzes both SPECrate and SPECspeed suites across pipeline, control flow, cache, and instruction mix behavior, including scale effects that appear at full system utilization. The authors frame the results as groundwork for workload-driven design of next-generation datacenter processors.

key_insights.text: The multi-lens analysis identifies three behavioral clusters: frontend control-flow-dominated workloads, high-efficiency compute workloads that suffer SMT contention at scale, and memory bandwidth-bound workloads with poor L3 filtering even at single-copy.
Scale-dependent effects such as SMT dispatch contention and L3 capacity interference emerge only at full system utilization and are not visible in conventional single-copy characterization.
The study is positioned as an empirical foundation for architectural research and design decisions for next-generation datacenter processors.

title: Exploiting the Benefits of V2B Application on Peak Shaving of Data Center Loads
author: Arya Joshi, Hamed Haggi, Chinmay Morankar
summary: This arXiv paper explores using Vehicle-to-Building (V2B) applications to shave peak cooling loads at data centers. It presents a conceptual simulation of a 10 MW data center in Loudoun County, VA, using 40 EVs, and reports that strategic V2B deployment between 12 and 5 pm could offset gross cooling loads by 13-36% depending on season.

key_insights.text: Simulated V2B deployment of 40 commercial and passenger EVs between 12-5pm offsets gross cooling loads by 13-36%, depending on seasonal cooling demand.
Using existing EV batteries as building-side energy assets could help data centers reduce peak grid demand and related carbon emissions.

title: Flexible Training Workloads in Large-Scale AI Data Centers for Transient-Stability Support in Transmission-Constrained Power Systems
author: Jae-Kyeong Kim
summary: The paper proposes training-induced load surge (TILS), a demand-side strategy that restarts or increases flexible AI training workloads in data centers after fault clearing to support transient stability. It evaluates the approach in a single-machine infinite-bus system, the IEEE 39-bus system, and a large-scale Korean power system, reporting increased transient-stability-constrained generation limits. Results depend on siting, response size, activation timing, and available electrical headroom.

key_insights.text: Upward load response from AI training workloads, activated after fault clearing, can reduce accelerating-power imbalance and limit first-swing rotor-angle excursion.
Siting data center load at buses with stronger electrical influence on critical generators gives larger generation-limit increases.
AI data center load flexibility could provide complementary transient-stability support to grid operators when electrical headroom and reliable grid-triggered activation exist.

title: 90 days of attacks on AI infrastructure
author: coder-pm
summary: Wiz Threat Research reports 90 days of honeypot telemetry showing active attacks on AI infrastructure, including LiteLLM, MCP servers and AI agent frameworks. The findings cover remote code execution through exposed MCP servers, blind prompt injection against agent frameworks, and AI-specific post-exploitation tooling.

key_insights.text: LiteLLM MCP Gateway authentication flaw (CVE-2026-59822) returns an unrestricted object when token validation fails, so any Bearer token grants full MCP access.
Command injection in LiteLLM MCP server test endpoints (CVE-2026-42271) lets attackers run arbitrary commands via the unvalidated command field.
A LiteLLM proxy often holds credentials for multiple model providers and may carry cloud IAM permissions, so one compromise can expose downstream services.

title: Redesigning the Inference Chip: From Nvidia GPU's Flaws to OpenAI Jalapeño

The excerpt says the author's team cut TTFT by 40% in a PD-disaggregated MaaS scenario by replacing the transport protocol with CIPU's eRDMA. The full article is truncated after its introduction.

key_insights.text: The author argues Nvidia's RoCE networking and DPU have performance and security defects, and that replacing the transport protocol with eRDMA cut TTFT by 40% in one PD-disaggregated scenario.

The author criticizes the L2 cache in Nvidia GPUs for consuming die area while adding 200~400 cycles of cross-partition latency to maintain UMA, and states that OpenAI's Jalapeño removes the L2 cache.
The author says a team without cloud operating experience would need at least five more years to mature in scale-in networking.

title: Minimizing Grid Interconnection Capacity Requirements for AI Data Centers: A Developer-Side Planning Framework with Onsite Resources and Workload Flexibility
author: Hassan Zahid Butt, Rida Fatima, Xingpeng Li
summary: The paper presents ICP-AI, a planning framework for AI data center developers that minimizes grid import capacity under an onsite investment budget by jointly sizing PV and battery storage and scheduling deadline-constrained workload flexibility. It reports capacity reductions of roughly 4.4% to 13.3% across budgets and load profiles, and checks temporal sensitivity by solving over a full 8,760-hour chronology.

key_insights.text: Securing grid interconnection capacity can take longer than constructing the facility, delaying AI data center deployment for years.
At a $10M budget, 5% flexible load with a 1 h deferral window reduces BESS capacity from 15.30 to 4.87 MWh while raising capacity reduction from 4.43% to 4.84%.
Interconnection capacity reduction depends strongly on the planning environment, reaching 13.3% for a more diurnal load at a $100M budget.
The framework provides an investment-interconnection frontier to support capital allocation and early project planning in constrained grid environments.

Support is limited to family-specific reference profiles, and some hybrid profiles call a helper Python executable.
Public-preview release wheels target Linux aarch64 only, with no published x86_64 wheels, which limits near-term deployment options for some teams.

title: Mitigating Forced Oscillations in Power Systems via Data-Enabled Predictive Control
author: Soraya Daabak, Verena Häberle, Gabriela Hug, Gustavo Valverde
summary: This arXiv paper proposes Data-Enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) to damp sustained forced oscillations in power systems, which the abstract says are driven by large cyclic loads such as data centers. The authors compare DeePC with a conventional power system stabilizer on a multi-machine two-area system and report superior damping that depends on dataset quality.

key_insights.text: Large cyclic loads such as data centers can drive sustained forced oscillations in power systems.
DeePC builds control actions from measured trajectories without an explicit system model, unlike fixed-parameter power system stabilizers.
DeePC effectiveness depends critically on the quality and representativeness of the historical data used in the Hankel matrix.

title: Current-Limiting Control for Fault Ride-Through of LLC-based Solid-State Transformer in Data Centers
author: Haoyu Wang, Chi Zhang, Mafu Zhang, Rudy Wang, Peter Barbosa
summary: This arXiv paper proposes a current-limiting and recovery control strategy for the DC-DC stage of a solid-state transformer (SST) that interfaces distribution grids with data centers. The method uses fault detection, a closed-loop current controller that adjusts switching frequency and duty cycle, and a ramped recovery, and is validated on an LLC converter prototype.

key_insights.text: A closed-loop current controller limits DC fault current within microseconds by raising switching frequency and adjusting duty cycle, without additional hardware.
A ramped recovery stage restores the DC bus after fault isolation without inrush current.
The approach aims to provide lower-cost fault response for resilient data center power architectures, avoiding extra hardware cost.

title: Who bears the risk in Nvidia's $500B financing platform?

The piece traces capital from insurance balance sheets through special purpose vehicles to neocloud and hyperscaler-linked borrowers, citing CoreWeave and Meta Hyperion debt as reference transactions.

key_insights.text: The announced $500 billion platforms are non-binding MOUs with no committed capital or per-partner allocation disclosed.
Incremental debt funded about 32% of hyperscaler capex on a trailing basis by mid-2026, up from about 9% in fiscal 2024.
GPUs are weak collateral for long-dated debt given a likely two-to-three-year competitive life versus five-to-six-year depreciation schedules.
Credit risk is argued to pass through SPVs into insurance balance sheets, where it is presented as investment-grade fixed income.

title: An Oversubscription and Service Pricing Exploitation-Based Profit Maximization Framework for Industry Cloud Resource Management
author: Deepika Saxena, Ashutosh Kumar Singh
summary: An arXiv paper proposes a cloud resource management framework that uses VM utilization prediction, fuzzy C-means clustering, and two pricing models to improve profit and efficiency for industry cloud providers. The authors report simulation results against benchmark VM traces, including reduced electricity bills, power consumption, and active servers.

key_insights.text: An ensemble machine learning model predicts VM resource utilization to reduce waste from oversubscription.
VMs with similar predicted usage are grouped with Fuzzy C-means clustering to determine the number of VMs to deploy.
The framework pairs Delay Sensitive and Best-Effort pricing models to maximize revenue and reduce electricity costs in cloud data centers.
Simulated results report electricity bill reductions and profit gains against state-of-the-art methods.

title: Cross-vendor byte-identical inference for a 72B LLM (AMD MI300X vs. Nvidia H100)
author: ashsyngh
summary: A self-published paper describes a protocol that produces byte-identical outputs from 72B-parameter LLM inference on NVIDIA H100 and AMD MI300X GPUs, binding each output to a signed, offline-verifiable receipt. It also describes a probabilistic spot-check verifier and reports benchmark and verification-cost results.

key_insights.text: Output hashes match byte-for-byte across fresh process launches in every measured configuration, and single-GPU bf16 eager-attention outputs are byte-identical between AMD and NVIDIA.
Two-GPU tensor-parallel outputs differ between NVIDIA and AMD, which the authors attribute to NCCL-ring versus RCCL-fabric all-reduce topology.
Receipts use a canonical CBOR schema with Ed25519 signatures, implemented in Go, Python, and Rust, and verification takes about 80 microseconds per receipt on a single core.

title: Next-generation O-RAN Edge: Energy-aware Joint Placement and Migration of Cloud-Native Functions
author: Nguyen Phuc Tran, Brigitte Jaumard, Oscar Delgado
summary: The paper studies energy-aware joint placement and migration of cloud-native functions in an O-RAN edge cloud, comparing single and multi CU-UP association models. It formulates a MILP to minimize server, transmission, wake-up, and migration energy under capacity and F1-U delay constraints in a fat-tree edge data center, and proposes a k-means heuristic. The authors report a 5.7% modeled energy reduction for the Multi-CU relaxation and a heuristic within about 9.7% of the MILP.

key_insights.text: A Multi-CU relaxation lets distinct slice-flow groups of one DU map to different CU-UP targets under one CU-CP.
A deterministic k-means heuristic approximates MILP placement decisions without repeated exact optimization.
The evaluated 24-hour workload shows a modeled 5.7% energy reduction for Multi-CU relative to Single-CU.

key_insights.text: Groq 3 LPX is designed to offload decode workloads from Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs, with up to 256 LP30 accelerators per rack-scale deployment.

title: Scalable datacenter replication with mostly-synchronous consensus on hardware

summary: An arXiv paper introduces scarHW, a network card design that implements a new consensus algorithm, POPUC, on an FPGA smartNIC to replicate data consistently at scale in datacenters. The authors report up to two orders of magnitude throughput and latency gains for Redis and Zookeeper compared with the state of the art, and state that the protocol was formally verified in TLA+.

key_insights.text: POPUC is implemented in an FPGA smartNIC to exploit the mostly synchronous behavior of programmable datacenter network devices.
The FPGA prototype improves throughput and latency of Redis and Zookeeper by up to two orders of magnitude relative to the state of the art, per the paper.
Consistent replication that scales with replica count could benefit datacenter services with stringent performance requirements.

key_insights.text: Jalapeño is designed as a general-purpose LLM inference chip rather than one tuned to OpenAI's own models, according to the article.
The article reports over 700 tokens per second per user at concurrency 1 on DeepSeek R1 using single-token prediction, without speculative decoding or prefill-decode disaggregation.
Design work reportedly began in mid-2024 and reached manufacturing tape-out in about 16 months, which the article describes as an extremely fast ASIC development cycle.

title: Loadability Limits Under Periodic Load Forcing
author: Maitraya Avadhut Desai, Gustavo Valverde, Gabriela Hug
summary: This arXiv letter studies loadability limits for power systems when part of the demand varies periodically, as with data-center loads. It shows the steady state becomes a forced periodic orbit whose loadability limit differs from the static limit and depends on forcing frequency.

key_insights.text: Under periodic load forcing, the generic instability is a cyclic fold of the orbit rather than a saddle-node of equilibria, so the limit depends on forcing frequency.
On a four-bus test system, a static margin of 2.5 p.u. shrinks to 0.53 p.u. near the swing frequency, and static analysis reproduces none of these effects.

title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
author: Jie Li, Chenxin Jia, Jinliang Shen, Cunzhuang Liu, Ruiyi Ding, Jianwen Xian, Kang He, Chengru Song
summary: The paper studies load balancing for expert-parallel MoE serving across GPUs, arguing that expert cost is neither linear in token count nor in activated experts alone, and proposes a max-affine cost profile. It presents TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher integrated with SGLang, reporting up to 15.5% gains where regimes mix and 4-6% throughput gains on Qwen3-235B end-to-end.

key_insights.text: Below roughly 156-168 tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates expert cost, so cost tracks activated replicas rather than tokens.
Above that threshold, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile M-tiles, so splitting an expert adds padded compute.
TEMPO's SGLang integration fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel and runs out-of-process.
End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B gains 4-6% throughput and about 15.6% lower p99 latency, while DeepSeek-V3 shows only mechanism cost.

It describes two operating regimes and validates the predictions on power-demand traces from three production data centers spanning HPC, GPU-training, and cloud workloads.

key_insights.text: Storage-assisted provisioning separates into a Small Battery Region, where storage nearly linearly reduces required power margin, and a Large Battery Region, where returns diminish.
Effective power, an analogue of effective bandwidth, is introduced to characterize required power in the Large Battery Region.
The framework is presented as a basis for dimensioning storage-assisted power provisioning in AI data centers.

title: InFactPlanner: Planning Sustainable Geo-Distributed LLM Data Centers

It estimates power, energy, carbon, water use, latency, and server utilization using query traces, hardware profiles, PUE/WUE parameters, renewable models, and grid carbon intensity. The authors report validation of their energy accounting within 10% of reference estimates and find that sustainability-optimal choices can differ from latency-optimal ones.

key_insights.text: The framework reproduces reference LLM inference energy estimates with less than 10% deviation.
Sustainability-optimal deployment choices can differ from latency-optimal ones.
The carbon value of a deployment depends strongly on the local grid mix.
Models compare site selection, capacity placement, hardware, renewable integration, and carbon-aware routing before infrastructure is built.

title: Nvidia Exemplar Cloud: Lessons for Unlocking Performance on AI Infrastructure
author: gmays
summary: NVIDIA describes debugging investigations into performance gaps of 8% to 12% between partner AI clusters built on H100, GB200 NVL72, or GB300 NVL72 systems and NVIDIA's reference architecture. The post walks through four case studies covering virtualization/SMMU, CPU power and NUMA placement, NCCL queue-pair concurrency on 1.6 Tbps fabrics, and hardware installation defects. It lists prerequisites and profiling tools such as Nsight Systems and nccl-tests.

key_insights.text: Configuration choices in the kernel, hypervisor, BIOS, and NCCL settings can each cost a few percent and compound into an 8% to 12% gap, enough to miss the 95% threshold for Exemplar Cloud validation.
A GB200 NVL72 partner deployment running DeepSeek-V3 MoE FP8 pre-training inside a VM ran iterations 12% to 14% slower than bare metal, while dense Llama 3 70B recipes ran within 3% of reference.
Exemplar Cloud validation requires reaching 95% of the NVIDIA reference architecture performance, making these tuning gaps directly relevant to partner cluster acceptance.

title: Techno-Economic Boundary Analysis of Small Modular Reactor Cogeneration for Hyperscale Data Center IT and Cooling Loads
author: Honglin Li, Buxin She, Jie Zhang
summary: An arXiv paper models co-optimized dispatch of a small modular reactor serving a 200 MWe data center in ERCOT, covering steam extraction, absorption cooling and grid exchange across 109 scenarios. It reports cost comparisons against grid supply under varying capital, market, policy and cooling-efficiency conditions.

key_insights.text: At 2023 mid-range reactor capital, nuclear configurations cost 49-62% more than grid supply even with the Section 45Y production tax credit.
Absorption cooling is dispatched in response to hourly electricity prices and supplies 38% of annual cooling, at an added cost of $9.2 million per year relative to the reactor-only plant.
A carbon price of $53-64 per tCO2 closes the mid-range cost gap under hourly export crediting.
The absorption cooling gap closes at an installed cost of $60/kWc at baseline efficiency and $570/kWc on a legacy-efficiency campus, versus surveyed commercial prices of $450-1,200/kWc.

title: The Abstention Protocol: RCA for Clos Fabrics
author: Madhava Gaikwad, Deepak Pandey
summary: An arXiv paper presents CoreSec, a root cause analysis system for large datacenter networks that replaces weighted score fusion with an abstention-based composition method. The authors report that it is deployed at hyperscale and gives stable, explainable attributions across Clos fabric environments.

key_insights.text: Root cause analysis in large datacenter networks is hard because telemetry is noisy, partial, and asynchronous.
CoreSec composes telemetry agents using control flags that yield deterministic decisions and explicit abstention when evidence is ambiguous.
Topology-aware configurations capture failure surfaces across Clos fabrics and converge as evidence accumulates.
The system is described as deployed at hyperscale and working across diverse environments without retuning.

title: ClusterBench: A Framework for Cluster-Wide Continuous Benchmarking and Regression Testing
author: Aditya Ujeniya, Jan Eitzinger, Thomas Gruber, Georg Hager, Gerhard Wellein
summary: The paper presents ClusterBench, a framework for cluster-wide continuous benchmarking that dispatches identical benchmarks to every node and repeats them over the cluster's lifetime to detect regressions. It reports on NHR@FAU clusters that performance variation within a component stays within 1%, while variation across nodes reaches 5%, and that the relation between performance and power, frequency, and temperature differs between air- and liquid-cooled nodes.

key_insights.text: Benchmarks are dispatched to every node in a single cluster-aware submission to validate an entire installation at acceptance and at regular intervals.
Repeated measurements are compared against earlier runs to detect performance regressions from software changes such as kernel updates or new library versions.
Cross-specimen performance variation reaches 5% on nodes identical by specification, while variation within a single component stays within 1%.
The performance-to-power, frequency, and temperature relationship differs between air-cooled and liquid-cooled nodes.

title: AIDC Microgrid Vulnerability Assessment Under Computing-Power Coordinated Attacks
author: Ze Yu, Hongwei Zhen, Chao Shen, Mingyang Sun
summary: The paper proposes an uncertainty-aware framework for assessing vulnerability of AI data center microgrids to coordinated attacks that combine adversarial AI requests altering power demand with inverter control tampering. Case studies report that coordinated attacks within identified critical windows cause sustained inverter frequency oscillations exceeding 20% of nominal frequency, while out-of-window responses remain bounded.

key_insights.text: Adversarial AI requests alter AIDC power demand while inverter control tampering modifies source-side dynamics, and their combined effect on stability depends on PV forecast and demand response uncertainty.
Impedance-based stability analysis is used to construct attack reachable domains and identify critical attack time windows.
Coordinated attacks within critical windows induce sustained inverter frequency oscillations with peak deviations above 20% of nominal frequency, whereas unlike single-component attacks.
Renewable integration for AI data centers strengthens coupling between AIDC loads and inverter-interfaced generation, creating cross-domain cyber-physical vulnerabilities.

title: PSP: Low-Overhead Packet-Level Load Balancing for Stale-State and Bandwidth-Asymmetric Networks
author: Jiaqi Liu, Chunyang Zhang, Heng Pan, Yanbiao Li
summary: The paper proposes probabilistic state-proportional (PSP) dispatching, a packet-level load balancing algorithm for multipath Clos networks in AI data centers. It uses a band-based discrete state representation to reduce hardware complexity and suppress herding caused by stale state information. Simulation results on a cycle-accurate simulator are reported as outperforming JSQ and Random and remaining competitive with Top-k.

key_insights.text: Traditional hash-based flow-level load balancing cannot sense link states, causing hash collisions, hotspot congestion and tail latency in Clos networks.
PSP replaces global sorting with local probability mapping using a band-based discrete state representation, reducing hardware complexity.
The authors claim PSP offers a lower hardware cost than Top-k while staying competitive on performance.

title: Do We Still Need Demand Flexibility as Batteries Become Cheaper? A Levelized Cost Perspective
author: Ruike Lyu, Tengmu Li
summary: An arXiv paper compares the levelized incremental cost of energy storage with industrial and data center load shifting as sources of flexibility for power systems with high variable renewable shares. It finds batteries suit short-cycle shifting, while load shifting becomes relatively cheaper for longer or seasonal flexibility periods.

key_insights.text: Energy storage cost per shifted kWh rises as the flexibility period lengthens and assets cycle less often.
Under representative central cost assumptions, batteries are more than 80 times more expensive than aluminum smelting load shifting for seasonal flexibility.
Load shifting does not share the capacity cost rise seen in storage under a fixed avoided-hour share, though new productive capacity can still be too costly.

title: Synthesizing Voltage Ride-Through Controllers for Data Centers
author: Wayne Wang, Archit Bhatnagar, Tongyuan Miao, Saniya Kalamkar, Wenqi Cui, Inigo Incer, Ang Chen
summary: An arXiv paper proposes SolVRT, a formal-methods system that synthesizes voltage ride-through controllers for data centers so they comply with grid codes. The approach encodes grid-code requirements in Signal Temporal Logic, and it diagnoses infeasible designs by identifying conflicting clauses and the smallest hardware or workload change needed. The authors report closed-loop simulations of a 200 MW data center connected to a 140-bus transmission system.

key_insights.text: Voltage ride-through grid codes require data centers to stay connected through grid disturbances, hold an active power floor, and recover draw within a deadline after restoration.
SolVRT encodes grid-code requirements in Signal Temporal Logic and synthesizes a correct-by-construction controller, or proves that none exists.
Simultaneous data center tripping during grid faults can destabilize the power system, motivating standardized VRT behavior.

title: Capacity Markets for Large Loads under Supply-Chain Constraints
author: Tong Liu, Jacob Mays
summary: An arXiv economics paper models bring-your-own-capacity mandates and flexibility accreditation in capacity markets for large loads such as data centers facing shared supply-chain constraints. It compares welfare effects of the two instruments under different supply-chain stress levels and price caps, and notes spillover and penalty-design implications.

key_insights.text: With efficient pricing, BYOC mandates mainly reallocate procurement between grid-built and self-built capacity and have little welfare effect.
Under administrative price caps, BYOC mandates can improve static welfare by forcing data centers to internalize the full cost of capacity.
Applying current capacity non-performance penalties to flexible loads may give financial incentives too weak to induce truthful flexibility reporting.

title: DC-CLM: Extending the WECC Composite Load Model for AI Data Center Dynamics
author: Md Kibria Saroare, Md Rubel Ahmed, Arif Hussain
summary: This arXiv paper presents DC-CLM, a workload-aware extension of the WECC composite load model that represents UPS-supported IT demand, motor and VFD cooling loads, and training, inference, and idle workload profiles. It is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and evaluated under fault-induced delayed voltage recovery for a study system with a 100 MW conventional load and a 200 MW data-center load. The authors report that training and inference produce larger voltage and active-power variation than idle operation in the first 100 ms after fault clearance.

key_insights.text: Long-duration voltage recovery under FIDVR is governed mainly by conventional stalled-motor thermal dynamics, while the first 100 ms after fault clearance is strongly workload-dependent.
Training and inference produce roughly 50-52 mpu voltage variation and 751-755 MW active-power variation, versus about 36 mpu and 654 MW for idle operation.

Incorporating data-center-specific load dynamics is presented as valuable for transmission-level stability studies, with measurement-based validation and converter-level modeling noted as future needs.

title: Keeping Data Centers Online in Weak Grids: PLL-Free VM-DPC With Adaptive Reactive-Power Support for Centralized UPS Systems
author: Jesus D. Vasquez-Plaza, Yonghao Gui, Jin Dong, Jamie Lian, Yilu Liu
summary: This arXiv paper studies stability of centralized UPS data center systems under weak-grid conditions using a switching-level Simulink model validated on OPAL-RT. It proposes a PLL-free voltage-modulated direct power control with adaptive reactive power support for the front-end rectifier, and reports that conventional PI control becomes unstable at SCR of 2 or less while the proposed method restores stable operation.

key_insights.text: Conventional PLL-based PI rectifier control can become unstable under weak-grid conditions due to interaction with grid impedance.
VM-DPC with adaptive reactive power support regulates active and reactive power without PLL synchronization and supports PCC voltage during rapid IT load changes.
Simulation and real-time OPAL-RT validation report conventional PI control unstable at SCR <= 2, with the proposed method restoring stable dc-link operation.

title: Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows

summary: This arXiv paper characterizes the architectural demands of agentic AI workflows, based on a production study at Microsoft Azure and a controlled study of open-source frameworks. key_insights.text: Agentic workflows repeatedly cross the CPU-GPU boundary, placing the CPU on the critical path because orchestration and tools run on the host.

The Agora prototype pools cores by role, uses affinity-aware scheduling, and prefetches agent state to hide GPU memory swap latency while preserving tail latency.
